jobs.title: Supply Chain Digital Readiness - Process Solutions Lead
jobs.excerpt: CHEP helps move more goods to more people, in more places than any other organization on earth via our 347 million pallets, crates and containers.
jobs.description:
CHEP helps move more goods to more people, in more places than any other organization on earth via our 347 million pallets, crates and containers. We employ approximately 13,000 people and operate in 60 countries. Through our pioneering and sustainable share-and-reuse business model, the world’s biggest brands trust us to help them transport their goods more efficiently, safely and with less environmental impact.

What does that mean for you? You’ll join an international organization big enough to take you anywhere, and small enough to get you there sooner. You’ll help change how goods get to market and contribute to global sustainability. You’ll be empowered to bring your authentic self to work and be surrounded by diverse and driven professionals. And you can maximize your work-life balance and flexibility through our Hybrid Work Model.

Job Description

Are you an engineering leader who thrives at the intersection of technology, operations, and continuous improvement? Do you enjoy solving complex challenges, influencing cross-functional teams, and driving the evolution of innovative solutions at scale? Join CHEP's Supply Chain Digital Readiness team as a Serialization (S+) Process Solutions Lead, where you'll play a pivotal role in advancing our S+ serialization ecosystem across North America and beyond. In this highly visible global role, you'll partner with engineering, operations, digital, and supplier teams to optimize processes, enhance equipment performance, lead pilot initiatives, and drive the successful scaling of cutting-edge serialization technologies. This is an opportunity to combine technical expertise, strategic thinking, and operational excellence to shape the future of supply chain innovation.

Key Responsibilities May Include:

  • Develop and manage large-scale capital engineering projects for automation, IoT and continuous improvement solutions, ensuring alignment with long-term business goals and objectives.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams (Operations, Health & Safety, Finance, Quality) and external suppliers to drive project success, managing stakeholders throughout the project lifecycle.
  • Lead the preparation of Capex documents, including cost estimates, project justifications, equipment layouts, and technical specifications, ensuring projects are delivered on time and within budget.
  • Manage equipment installation and commissioning, including contractor supervision, safety compliance, and ensuring adherence to all environmental regulations and legislative requirements.
  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives aimed at reducing Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF) and increasing operational efficiency through the adoption of advanced technologies like AI, robotics, and digital twin models.
  • Ensure the development and delivery of proper training programs and operational documentation (as-built drawings, manuals, spare parts lists) to ensure seamless handover to operational teams.
  • Maintain strict financial control over capital projects, accurately forecasting expenditures, managing budgets, and ensuring fiduciary compliance throughout project execution.
  • Champion Zero Harm and environmental standards, ensuring projects meet the highest safety requirements and adhere to regulatory standards throughout the project lifecycle.

The S+ Process Solutions Lead will lead and evolve the processes and technology driving S+ (our tag-based serialization ecosystem) in the Service Centers and other pallet-handling locations. This role will work closely with the Chile and North America regional business teams, as well as the global teams in Technology Services (TS), Digital and Supply Chain (SC) Engineering to lead the development, standardization, implementation and continuous improvement of the processes, technology and infrastructure driving S+.

The S+ Process Solutions Lead will also be the principal Process Owner sitting within Global Supply Chain for those parts of the end-to-end process that support the running of the of S+ ecosystem (i.e. equipment, infrastructure, and software solutions) in the service centers and other physical locations. Within this scope is leading the continuous optimization of the processes through developments leveraging the data coming directly and indirectly from the S+ pallet scans to create incremental savings value in SC.

This position requires up to 50% across North and South America. Candidates must live near a major US airport.


Other Responsibilities Include:

  • Work with local and global teams to lead and co-ordinate the developments of the equipment and software arising from the continuous improvement and product lifecycle processes (Digital, Technology Services, North America SC team and the Chile SC team)
  • Coordinate and lead the site-based S+ Proof of Concept and Pilot project activities between the involved teams, both regionally and globally
  • Measure and report the success of trials and test activities to product lifecycle governance bodies, giving your opinion on next steps and future actions
  • Taking input from various stakeholders, define the global ramp-up and run metrics for the S+ equipment and processes
  • With Digital and other teams, develop scorecards, tracking and follow-up processes for the S+ equipment to ensure ramp-up and run targets are met
  • Track the expansion of the processes and equipment across North America and Chile and prepare and deliver progress updates.
  • Lead the definition and documentation of the global operating processes for the S+ equipment in the service centers
  • Drive the local teams to identify process and equipment improvements and turn these ideas into projects with the central teams, creating and documenting requirements and preparing the necessary project documents
  • Drive the local Engineering teams to ensure maintenance and repair processes are suitably documented
  • Validate that the assumptions and measures used to calculate the Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) are appropriate and values used are correct in each TCO update cycle

Experience – What you’ll Bring

  • Engineering degree (Mechanical, Electrical, Electromechanical preferred)
  • Process Engineering and Product development in Supply Chain/Manufacturing
  • 10+ years in manufacturing, supply chain, industrial operations, automation, or logistics environments
  • Experience leading technical projects from problem identification through implementation
  • Process ownership mindset with end-to-end systems thinking
  • Experience collaborating across engineering, operations, digital, and vendor teams
  • Strong stakeholder influence without direct authority
  • Experience driving continuous improvement initiatives
  • Comfortable operating in complex global environments
  • Program/project management capability
  • Able to translate operational issues into technical requirements

Desirable Skills

  • Electromechanical backgrounds strongly desired
  • Machine vision, automation, industrial equipment, scanning, serialization, RFID, labeling, or tracking technologies
  • Spanish language capability highly desirable
  • Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen exposure
  • Product lifecycle or industrialization experience
  • Supply chain transformation experience
  • Experience creating SOPs, playbooks, or scalable operating standards
  • Financial/TCO optimization experience

What we Offer:  

  • Competitive Pay + Annual Bonus
  • Benefits Day 1!  
  • 401K w/ company match (up to 4%) 
  • FREE company-paid vision, short-term disability, and life insurance!! 
  • Employee Stock Match Program!
  • Tuition reimbursement, parental leave, childcare assistance, profit sharing, and MORE! 

Remote Type

Fully Remote

Skills to succeed in the role

Adaptability, Empathy, Experimentation, Taking Ownership, Teamwork, Understand Customers

Training Strategy & Leadership

  • Create certification programs that align with promotion pathways and role requirements

  • Partner with compliance and regulatory teams to ensure adherence to industry standards, especially in MedTech environments

  • Support audit readiness through proper documentation and reporting

  • Work closely with Sales Leaders to embed training into daily workflows and reinforce learning in the field

  • Support change management and salesforce effectiveness with training strategies and enablement materials

  • Demonstrated success in curriculum development, training content creation, and facilitation

  • Proven experience identifying sales performance gaps and implementing targeted development programs

  • Strong background in training delivery (live, virtual, and blended learning environments)

  • Experience managing training programs, including tracking, compliance, and reporting

  • Excellent communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills

  • Ability to influence and partner effectively with Sales Leadership

  • MedTech, healthcare, or medical device sales experience strongly preferred

Thriveworks is currently seeking Licensed Clinicians to provide telehealth sessions in Alabama.

About the job
Thriveworks is a mental health care company founded by clinicians in 2008 and still led by them today. With 340+ locations and a nationwide hybrid care model, we serve over 175,000 clients annually through more than 1.7 million sessions, and we're growing. In addition to working directly with clients, we partner with health systems and primary care providers because we believe mental health is inseparable from physical health. As a clinician-led organization, we're built to support the people who do this work with the tools, community, and stability you need to build a career that lasts.

About the Role
We’re hiring licensed clinicians to provide compassionate, evidence-based care to our more than 175,000 clients across the country. You may be a good fit for this role if you’re:

  • Independently licensed and living in Alabama — LPC, LMFT, LICSW, LP (Licensed Psychologist)

  • Consistently available to clients for a minimum of 25 sessions with 30 hours of availability weekly

  • A behavioral health generalist who is open to treating a variety of clients, including couples and children

  • Invested in helping your clients achieve measurable progress

  • Confident working with modern clinical technology, including telehealth and EHR tools

  • A good teammate — we’re building a clinical community and value positive contributors

Compensation
Up to $100,300 based on licensure type, session volume, and bonus opportunities. Full-time clinicians are eligible for health insurance, student loan repayment assistance, paid time off, and other employer-sponsored benefits.

How We Support You
We handle the administrative work so you can focus on what you do best: providing exceptional care. That means credentialing, billing, scheduling, and marketing support taken care of for you, plus paid orientation and training to get you started. You'll build a full caseload within 90 days of credentialing, with flexible scheduling available seven days a week from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. ET.

Benefits
As a W2 employee, you'll be eligible to receive:

  • Guaranteed bi-weekly pay for completed sessions

  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage

  • 401(k) with employer matching

  • Paid time off

  • Short- and long-term disability insurance

  • Company-paid life and AD&D insurance

  • CEU reimbursement and free in-house training

  • Student loan repayment assistance

  • Opportunities for paid clinical supervisor roles in select states

Our Community
Being a clinician can feel isolating, especially in a telehealth world. We're built to make sure it doesn't. You'll have access to live clinical support, monthly case consultations, and a vibrant online and in-person community of more than 2,700 licensed providers. All clinical leadership is promoted from within, so the people supporting you have been exactly where you are.

Ready to Join Us?
Apply today to become part of a team that’s changing mental health care for clients and clinicians alike.


Interested in joining Team Thriveworks? We're thrilled to meet you!


With Job scams becoming more and more frequent, here's how to know you're speaking with a real member of our team:

  • Our recruiters and other team members will only email you from or an @thriveworks.com email address.

350.org is looking for a Field Organizer who can build and grow the climate movement and 350 Japan’s volunteer community.

About 350.org

350’s mission is to keep carbon in our atmosphere to a safe level, below 350 parts per million. We do this by mobilizing ordinary people to campaign for universal access to clean energy and an end to fossil fuels. Our campaigns are rooted in local organizing, so that while achieving measurable reductions in fossil fuel emissions, we also build the power and potential of the climate movement for yet more impact to come. The values that guide and drive our work are listed here.

350.org is an equal opportunity employer. 350.org strives to be an inclusive and collaborative group of people who bring a variety of approaches to the work we do. We’re committed to the principles of justice, and we try to build a safe workplace where everyone is treated fairly and enjoys working together. We value new perspectives, ideas of all sorts, and different ways of working. Diverse perspectives and experiences improve the way 350.org carries out our work – including what we decide to work on and how creatively/effectively we do that. We do our best to make staff positions accessible to all potential team members, regardless of race, national origin, ethnicity, age, disability, assigned gender, gender expression or identity, sexual orientation or identity, religion or creed, veteran status, marital or parental status, and genetic information. We also strive to include team members in communities most impacted by climate change or impacted by other kinds of environmental, social, and economic injustice.

About the Field Organizer

The Field Organizer carries out defined parts of 350 Japan’s organizing work, under the guidance of the line manager, and helps grow the grassroots climate movement in Japan. Working closely with the line manager, they build a volunteer community, recruit individuals and groups, and support new leaders. They also run and help design training that helps activists take part in 350 Japan's campaigns in ways that fit Japan's cultural context. They support assigned projects and workstreams, as directed by the line manager, and contribute ideas to the organizing strategy. The role is based in Japan, with a preference for the Kanto area. Native-level Japanese and business-level English are required. If we don't find a candidate who matches this profile, we will consider people with different experience, language skills, and expertise. We encourage everyone to apply, whether or not they meet every requirement listed here.

Duties and Responsibilities

Strategy & Campaign Execution

  • Assist in implementing 350 Japan's organizing strategy as directed by the line manager and contribute ideas to its development.
  • Support delivery of assigned parts of short- and long-term organizing for campaigns, global moments, and key projects, from planning through to evaluation.

Community Building & Leadership Support

  • Maintain and grow the 350 crew and volunteer community toward 350 Japan's campaign goals.
  • Support activist leaders, taking direct responsibility for some of them.

Training & Development

  • Deliver training for individuals, groups, and leaders, both existing programs and new ones.
  • Contribute to improving training content, keeping it in line with campaign goals and culturally relevant.

Recruitment & Movement Growth

  • Find, engage, and recruit new participants to the movement.
  • Spot emerging leaders and support their growth.

Public Engagement

  • Engage with the general public to raise awareness and recruit new volunteers and activists.
  • Support relationships with existing groups and movements so we can take joint action for climate justice.

Collaboration & Learning

  • Work with, contribute to, and learn from teams beyond Japan, especially the Asia team and the global organizers' community.

Accountability & Reporting

  • Give your line manager timely updates on progress, challenges, and lessons learned.

Required Qualifications

Passion & Commitment

  • A strong passion for addressing climate change and a basic understanding of the issue.
  • A deep commitment to building a joyful, inclusive movement grounded in justice, equity, diversity, and inclusion.

Organizing & Leadership

  • Ability to plan and deliver organizing activities with regular guidance, and to support small projects
  • Willingness to learn, adapt, and grow as an organizer.
  • Self-motivation and the ability to work remotely, effectively, and sustainably with regular check-ins with the line manager.

Collaboration & Communication

  • A kind, collaborative team player who values accountability.
  • Good written and verbal communication skills, both inside and outside the organization.
  • Ability to identify problems and propose solutions for the line manager’s decision
  • Comfortable using, or willing to learn, digital organizing tools such as CRM (ActionKit), Google Workspace, Slack, Zoom, LINE, Canva, and Instagram.

Language

  • Native-level Japanese.
  • Business-level English.

Desired (but not required) skills and experiences

  • 2+ years of professional organizing experience, or 1+ year in climate-focused professional movement organizing.
  • Experience facilitating workshops or trainings.

When you join the team as an Executive Care Coordinator, you'll have the opportunity to make a difference in the lives of our patients each day as they look to you as part of their dedicated support team for helping them navigate the tricky process of getting access to their complex medication. You'll compassionately deliver an exceptional experience to many patients per day, always remembering that every prescription or document belongs to a real person who is looking for thorough and efficient management of their records. You'll adjust your approach to their needs by communicating clearly, focusing on the accuracy of the details of their medical records, your mastery of the program requirements, and ensuring their prescriptions or cases are handled in a timely manner. An Executive Care Coordinator has the ability to translate knowledge into patient friendly language and education.


A typical day in this role will include ownership of your patient journey from initiation to closure by using your critical thinking skills and your knowledge of the program and industry rules and standards. This includes completing benefit investigations, tracking prior authorizations / denial appeals, and assisting patients or other callers/stakeholders through resolution (via email, inbound/outbound calls and using our patented technology, Lynk). This role requires a strong understanding of pharmacy and medical billing and coding, excellent communication skills, and the ability to navigate complex reimbursement processes.


The Executive Care Coordinator provides expertise on insurance coverage and common access and reimbursement challenges affecting patients, healthcare providers and clients. The Executive Care Coordinator responsibilities include education on the access and reimbursement support tools available from Valeris and participating program, advising HCPs and/or patients and caregivers on the benefits and program eligibility for a specific patient, and educating HCP offices on Payor processes and procedures.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Relationship Management
    • Builds trusted relationships with patients, prescribers, and appropriate client stakeholders regarding reimbursement inquiries and challenges through proactive communication, timely and accurate execution of deliverables and demonstrated relentless passion for helping patients.

    • Managed through call/contact center structure, this role supports inbound and outbound calls to patients, caregivers, specialty pharmacies and healthcare professionals.
    • Performs post Benefits Investigation calls to patients and/or physicians explaining coverage options and next steps in the access journey.
    • Manages all client inquiries as appropriate, such as case specific statuses.
    • Manages HCP inquiries, as applicable, pursuant to business rules.
  • All communications with the client’s field teams will remain compliant and adhere to ways of working protocols outlined between Valeris and the client teams. Inbound Call Management
    • Manages inbound calls as directed by the program-approved FAQs
    • Triage patients to internal or external resources as appropriate.
  • Personalized Case Management
    • Provides personalized case management to patients and HCPs including outbound communication to HCPs, specialty pharmacies and patients to communicate benefit coverage and/or appropriately help drive next steps in obtaining coverage and/or access to prescribed medicine. All communications for case management will follow the guidelines set forth for the program and only provide information publicly available and/or outlined in the patient insert.
    • Leverages electronic tools to identify benefits and payer coverage; completes manual benefit investigation as needed.
    • Identifies and communicates patient’s plan benefit coverage including the need for prior authorization, appeal, tier exception, and/or formulary exclusions.
    • Serves as a subject matter expert to internal team as required and appropriate.
    • Uses electronic resources to obtain benefit coverage outcome and if needed, outbound call to payers and HCPs to follow up on proper submission and/or outcome.
    • Coordinates nurse teach with nurse educators, as applicable to program.
    • Supports adherence services as applicable to program.
    • Identifies peer support resources for patients.
    • Proactively communicates needs for reverification of prior authorization or re-enrollment.
    • Identifies and reports adverse events, product complaints, special situation reports and/or medical inquiries received in accordance with program operating procedures and the Business Rules.
    • Documents all activities within the Lynk system, maintaining detailed records of reimbursement activities, including claims status, payments, and appeals.
    • Generate reports and analysis as needed to identify trends and opportunities for improvement.in accordance with business requirements.
  • Utilize Valeris’ values as the driving force behind the team’s success
  • On time adherence to training deadlines for all corporate policies and procedures
  • Ensure all SOPs are followed with consistency
  • Perform additional tasks or projects as assigned

Qualifications:

  • Must be fluent in both Spanish and English languages.
  • Completion of Bachelor's degree (or higher) required. Degree in healthcare administration, social science or similar related fields is strongly preferred. In lieu of a degree, five plus years of experience in insurance reimbursement, patient access, direct patient care, and/or patient education is required.
  • Two years of experience in insurance reimbursement, patient access, direct patient care, and/or patient education is required.
  • Minimum two years of experience in healthcare access delivery or management is strongly preferred.
  • Will consider other certifications and five or more consecutive years of experience in relevant field. Certification examples include PACS (Prior Authorization Certified Specialist), CHES (Certified Health Education Specialist) or CCM in healthcare or social science (Certified Case Manager).
  • Strong understanding of medical terminology, coding systems (ICD-10, CPT, HCPCS), and insurance processes.
  • Demonstrated examples of executing within guardrails recognizing urgency and consistently delivering patient centric results.
  • Excellent attention to detail and organizational skills.
  • Ability to prioritize tasks and work efficiently in a fast-paced environment.
  • Effective written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to interact professionally with diverse stakeholders.
  • Demonstrates the ability to think critically and issue resolution.
  • Knowledge of healthcare compliance regulations, including HIPAA and Medicare/Medicaid guidelines.

Physical Demands & Work Environment

We’re committed to supporting the well-being and success of our team members. As part of our organization, full-time employees can expect:

Job Summary:

The Tech Lead Data Scientist, AI Evaluation & Monitoring is the principal technical expert for how Geisinger evaluates, monitors, and optimizes AI systems in production. This is a hands-on technical leadership role. The Tech Lead sets the technical direction for AI evaluation across a large and growing portfolio, provides technical leadership to a team of data analysts who execute evaluation work, and partners directly with AI program teams to raise the quality of how AI is validated, monitored, and improved over time.

The role exists because AI at Geisinger has scaled past the point where oversight can be a document-review exercise. We need a technical leader who can guide program teams toward better-designed evaluations up front, instrument meaningful production monitoring, and continually advance the methods we use, from LLM-as-Judge frameworks to simulation-based testing to pragmatic experiment design that actually scales in healthcare.

Job Duties:

What You Will Own:

  • The technical evaluation methodology applied to AI programs across the enterprise, pre-production validation, production monitoring, and ongoing optimization
  • Hands-on guidance to program teams as they design validation studies, equity audits, monitoring plans, and escalation playbooks for their AI systems
  • Instrumentation of production monitoring: translating program-specific failure modes into concrete, measurable metrics
  • The evaluation toolkit: LLM-as-Judge frameworks, golden sets, simulation harnesses, experimental study designs, drift detection, subgroup fairness analysis
  • Reusable evaluation playbooks and templates that let each new program move faster than the last
  • Technical direction, design review, and mentorship for a team of data analysts supporting the evaluation function

What You Will Not Own:

  • People management, HR administration, or formal performance evaluations for the analyst team (those sit with the analysts' line manager; the Tech Lead provides technical input)
  • Program-level product strategy or go/no-go decisions
  • Final clinical validation judgment on whether a given AI is safe for a given clinical use
  • The software infrastructure behind the evaluation and monitoring tooling (built by the AI Platform team — the Tech Lead defines what's measured and how; Platform builds the backend)

Shape of the Work:

This is a role that lives at three altitudes at once:

With program teams (hands-on advisory). Partner with program owners early, before evaluations are designed, to shape study approach, sample size, stratification, gold-standard definition, and decision thresholds. Translate ambiguous failure modes into concrete, defensible evaluation designs. Coach teams through the technical work so that what arrives at governance review is rigorous, not performative.

With the evaluation toolkit (hands-on build). Design and operate the reusable assets that let evaluation scale: LLM-as-Judge rubrics and calibration methods, golden sets, simulation harnesses, A/B and shadow-mode study templates, subgroup fairness analyses, and drift monitors. Keep a pragmatic eye on what actually works in a clinical environment versus what works in a paper.

With the analyst team (technical leadership). Set technical direction, assign work across active evaluations, review analysis code and study designs, and raise the technical bar. Mentor analysts on methodology, statistical rigor, and the domain knowledge that makes evaluation credible. Grow them from execution into independent evaluation design.

Methods You'll Use:

  • Experimental and quasi-experimental design for production AI systems
  • LLM and generative AI evaluation: golden sets, judge-based evaluation, hallucination and grounding checks
  • Fairness and equity evaluation across patient and stakeholder subgroups
  • Production monitoring design: drift detection, performance decay, adoption, and outcome metrics
  • Causal inference methods appropriate to healthcare settings where full RCTs are often impractical
  • Simulation and adversarial testing for pre-production stress testing
  • Python, SQL, modern ML and evaluation tooling, cloud-native data platforms

Work is typically performed in an office or remote environment. Accountable for satisfying all job specific obligations and complying with all organization policies and procedures. The specific statements in this profile are not intended to be all-inclusive. They represent typical elements considered necessary to successfully perform the job.

*Relevant experience may be a combination of related work experience and degree obtained (Master's Degree = 2 years; PHD = 4 years ).

Position Details:

Required Skills & Qualifications:

  • 6+ years in data science, statistics, ML engineering, or applied quantitative research, with demonstrated experience as the senior technical voice on cross-functional projects

  • Strong foundation in experimental design and causal inference — and judgment about which method fits which situation

  • Hands-on experience designing and running model evaluation studies in real production settings

  • Experience evaluating LLM or generative AI systems, or comparable experience evaluating complex ML systems where ground truth is messy

  • Proven ability to translate ambiguous failure modes into concrete, defensible evaluation designs and monitoring metrics

  • Strong fluency in Python and SQL; working comfort with modern ML tooling and cloud-native data environments

  • Experience with fairness and equity evaluation for ML systems

  • Track record of providing technical leadership and mentorship without formal people-management authority

  • Clear written communication — the role produces evaluation memos and specifications that non-technical decision-makers rely on

  • Healthcare, clinical, or regulated-industry experience strongly preferred

  • MS or PhD in a quantitative field preferred; equivalent experience accepted

Education:

Bachelor's Degree-Related Field of Study (Required)

Experience:

Minimum of 6 years-Relevant experience* (Required)

Certification(s) and License(s):

Skills:

Analyzing, processing and building AI/ML solutions from Clinical and Operational data sources, such as Epic Clarity, HL7, DICOM, or ECG data, Clinical Databases, Communication, Critical Thinking, Data Analysis, Data Presentations, Group Collaboration, Leadership, Machine Learning Methods, Programming Languages, Structured Query Language (SQL)

OUR PURPOSE & VALUES: Everything we do is about caring for our patients, our members, our students, our Geisinger family and our communities.

  • KINDNESS: We strive to treat everyone as we would hope to be treated ourselves.
  • EXCELLENCE: We treasure colleagues who humbly strive for excellence.
  • LEARNING: We share our knowledge with the best and brightest to better prepare the caregivers for tomorrow.
  • INNOVATION: We constantly seek new and better ways to care for our patients, our members, our community, and the nation.
  • SAFETY: We provide a safe environment for our patients and members and the Geisinger family.

We offer healthcare benefits for full time and part time positions from day one, including vision, dental and domestic partners. Perhaps just as important, we encourage an atmosphere of collaboration, cooperation and collegiality.

We know that a diverse workforce with unique experiences and backgrounds makes our team stronger. Our patients, members and community come from a wide variety of backgrounds, and it takes a diverse workforce to make better health easier for all. We are proud to be an affirmative action, equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment regardless to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or status as a protected veteran.

jobs.description:
At MoneyGram, we're combining the strength of a trusted global brand with the agility of a tech-forward, growth driven culture. With 80+ years of experience and a presence in more than 200 countries and territories, we've built a foundation of stability and trust to help millions of people around the world send funds quickly, securely, and affordably. We're looking for bold thinkers, builders, technologists, and sellers who want real ownership of their work, thrive in collaborative environments, and are energized by solving complex challenges. Here, you'll have the opportunity to make a measurable impact - fast. If you're eager to shape the future of cross-border payments and financial services, join us as we transform how the world moves money.

At MoneyGram, we connect the world by making cross-border money transfers seamless, affordable, and secure for everyone. We are seeking an Implementation Coordinator. This role is responsible for executing and managing onboarding workflows for partner applications and existing partner modifications. This role ensures that applications progress efficiently through automated due diligence and partner configuration processes, while maintaining high standards of accuracy, compliance, and operational discipline.

What you will get to do:

Workflow Execution & Monitoring

  • Execute end-to-end onboarding workflows for assigned partners, ensuring timely progression through each stage
  • Monitor application status across systems and proactively address delays or bottlenecks
  • Ensure all required steps are completed in accordance with defined processes and SLAs
  • Monitor performance of new partners through established timeline

Automation & System Interaction

  • Utilize automated tools for due diligence, validation, and partner configuration setup
  • Review system outputs for completeness and accuracy, identifying exceptions or discrepancies
  • Trigger appropriate workflows and actions based on system results

Data Accuracy & Documentation

  • Validate partner information and ensure data integrity across platforms
  • Maintain complete and audit-ready documentation aligned with compliance requirements
  • Ensure all onboarding records are properly captured within internal systems

Issue Identification & Escalation

  • Identify missing information, inconsistencies, or process breakdowns
  • Escalate issues to senior team members with clear context and supporting details
  • Support resolution of workflow blockers to maintain onboarding momentum

Operational Support

  • Collaborate with internal teams (Compliance, Operations, Credit, Treasury) to support onboarding activities
  • Contribute to continuous improvement by identifying inefficiencies in workflows or systems

Other duties as assigned.

Who you are:

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree preferred, or equivalent combination of education and experience in business, compliance, or technical fields.

Experience

  • 1+ years of experience in operations, onboarding, or financial services (preferred)
  • Experience in payments, fintech, or remittance environments is a plus
  • Familiarity with workflow tools, CRM systems, or onboarding platforms

Key Skills

  • Bilingual fluency required, including professional-level English communication (written and verbal).
  • Strong operational judgment and problem-solving skills
  • Ability to make decisions within structured guidelines
  • High attention to detail and data accuracy
  • Ability to manage multiple workflows in a fast-paced environment
  • Effective communication and stakeholder coordination skills
  • Comfort working with automated systems and interpreting system outputs

About MoneyGram MoneyGram is a global payments network built to move money across borders with speed, simplicity and trust. Its omnichannel platform empowers consumers, developers and agents to transfer cash, fiat and stablecoin however it works best for them. The company serves over 50 million customers a year across 200+ countries and territories, nearly half a million retail locations and a rapidly expanding digital ecosystem reaching billions of devices. As one of the most recognized and trusted names in global payments, MoneyGram continues to reinvent how money moves - helping people around the world support their loved ones and build better futures.

Job Description

Ready to start a career with Global Payments?


As a Supplier Enrollment Specialist and play a key role in expanding our virtual card payment network. In this fast-paced, customer-focused role, you'll partner with suppliers, educate them on the benefits of virtual payments, and help drive adoption of innovative payment solutions that create value for businesses across the globe.

What you'll own

  • Research, qualify, and enroll suppliers into MineralTree's virtual card payment program through high-volume outbound outreach.
  • Educate suppliers on the benefits of accepting virtual card payments and becoming part of our payment network.
  • Identify and overcome objections through active listening, consultative conversations, and professional communication.
  • Guide suppliers through the enrollment process while delivering an exceptional customer experience.
  • Gather and validate required supplier information accurately and efficiently to ensure successful enrollment.
  • Consistently exceed weekly and monthly enrollment, performance, and quality assurance goals.
  • Maintain a high level of self-motivation while managing outbound calling activity and achieving results with minimal supervision.
  • Cross-train and support additional functions within the Payment Optimization and Payment Operations teams as needed.
  • Evaluate business processes and recommend improvements that enhance efficiency and customer satisfaction.
  • Support onboarding and training efforts for new team members as the organization continues to grow.

What you'll bring

  • 1-3 years of outbound sales, business development, or customer engagement experience.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills.
  • Strong presentation and relationship-building abilities.
  • Customer-focused mindset with outstanding attention to detail.
  • High degree of energy, accountability, and self-motivation.
  • Excellent problem-solving skills and resourcefulness.
  • Ability to manage objections and influence outcomes through consultative conversations.
  • Strong integrity and professionalism in all interactions.
  • Experience using CRM platforms such as Salesforce.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint.
  • Desire to contribute to a fast-growing, collaborative, and high-performance culture.

It's a bonus if you have

  • B2B sales experience.
  • Experience within virtual card, ePayables, commercial card, merchant processing, payments, procurement, or fintech industries.
  • Demonstrated track record of consistently exceeding performance goals and targets.
  • Experience in high-volume outbound calling environments.
  • Knowledge of supplier enablement, payment optimization, or accounts payable solutions.
  • Experience mentoring or training new team members.

About the team

The Payment Optimization team helps customers unlock greater value from their payment programs by expanding supplier participation in virtual card and electronic payment solutions. Through proactive outreach, consultative conversations, and a commitment to customer success, the team drives enrollment growth while delivering an exceptional experience for suppliers and customers alike. This is a highly collaborative environment where initiative, curiosity, and results are recognized and rewarded.

If you're looking for an opportunity to grow your career while making an impact in the evolving world of payments, we'd love to meet you.

Job Description

The Opportunity

The College of Arts & Sciences (COAS) at Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University–Worldwide Campus (ERAU-W) seeks a tenure-track assistant professor with a Ph.D. in Criminology, Criminal Justice, Homeland Security, Security Studies, or a related field.

This is a fully remote online position (U.S.-based) with no relocation required; travel will be required to attend commencement and mandatory college meetings as well as relevant other events.

Candidates will hold a Ph.D. in Criminology, Criminal Justice, Homeland Security, Sociology, Security Studies or a related field and have an active, pertinent scholastic research agenda.

The Department of Emergency, Disaster and Global Security Studies, includes the following degree programs: M.S. Human Security and Resilience, M.S. Emergency Services, M.S. Security and Intelligence Studies, B.S. Homeland Security, B.S. Emergency Services, A.S. in Emergency Management, as well as minors in Security Studies, Military Science, International Relations, Criminal Justice, Homeland Security and Emergency Services. Faculty are active scholars in their disciplines and collaborators across the college and with external partners.

The successful candidate will teach in several of the above programs based on their qualifications. The position will also oversee the newly launched Criminal Justice minor and teach related courses. Teaching modalities primarily include asynchronous and synchronous online delivery. A limited number of face-to-face offerings may be available based on faculty location.

The successful candidate will maintain an exemplary level of research and scholarly activity. ERAU offers a variety of internal research support programs, including college- and university-level funding opportunities. Service responsibilities for this candidate are likely to include contributing to student success through recruitment and retention efforts, administering the Criminal Justice minor and other curriculum and program development, as well as participation on departmental, college, and/or university committees.

About the College of Arts & Sciences

Based on its Strategic Guidance, the College of Arts & Sciences at ERAU-W develops and supports career- ready graduates and advances all students to be lifelong learners and leaders in their professional disciplines. The college’s vision is to be a destination for multidisciplinary studies and impactful collaborative research as well as continue to be a national leader in general education, developing opportunities for our diverse student population to fulfill their educational goals and become responsive, responsible global citizens.

The college comprises four departments: Emergency, Disaster and Global Security Studies; Human Factors, Safety and Social Sciences ; Humanities and Communication; and Mathematics, Science, and Technology.

The college delivers courses online as well as on several sites across the United States and around the world. Currently, four graduate and seven undergraduate programs are offered, as well an several combined undergraduate-graduate pathways programs and undergraduate minors.

The college also delivers the general education program to all Worldwide Campus students, providing over 2,000 sections annually, with a focus on developing students’ capacity in critical thinking, quantitative reasoning, information literacy, communication, scientific literacy, cultural literacy, technological literacy, and collaboration. The Worldwide Campus has an enrollment of more than 23,000 students, delivering courses globally online via Canvas, synchronously via EagleVision to both homes and classrooms, face-to-face at over 130 locations, and in a blended format.

Embry-Riddle's Worldwide Campus has earned a top five ranking during the past nine years for Best Online Bachelor’s programs from U.S. News & World Report.

About us

For over 100 years, Embry-Riddle has been the world's leading aviation and aerospace university, educating more than 30,000 students across residential campuses in Daytona Beach, Florida, and Prescott, Arizona, as well as through a global network of Worldwide locations and online programs. With more than 165,000 alumni around the world, our impact reaches every corner of the aerospace, aviation, defense and technology industries.

Today, our faculty, researchers and professional staff are advancing innovation across aviation, space, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, autonomous systems and next-generation engineering. Working alongside industry leaders, government agencies and innovators, they are solving real-world challenges and shaping the technologies that will define tomorrow.

Whether you are an educator, researcher, administrator, technologist or industry professional, your work at Embry-Riddle will contribute to something bigger than a job. Join a community driven by discovery, purpose and excellence—and help shape the future of aerospace.

Perks Await You at Embry-Riddle!

  • Generous Time Off: Enjoy 9+ paid holidays, including the day after Thanksgiving and the week between Christmas Eve and New Year’s Day.

  • Tuition Coverage: Get 100% tuition coverage for yourself for one undergraduate and one graduate degree, and discounted rates for your spouse and dependent children up to age 26.

  • Retirement Contributions: ERAU contributes 6% of your base salary to your retirement plan and offers a 4% matching contribution – with no vesting period.

Qualifications

Required Education and Qualifications:

  • Ph.D. in Criminology, Criminal Justice, Homeland Security, Sociology, Security Studies or a related field

Preferred qualifications:

  • Applicants with a specialization in criminal justice, homeland security, or an area that complements the research and teaching expertise of the current faculty in the department.

Review of applications will begin immediately and will continue until the position is filled.

jobs.description:
PATH current employees - please log in and apply Here

PATH is a global nonprofit dedicated to achieving health equity. With more than 40 years of experience forging multisector partnerships and with expertise in science, economics, technology, advocacy, and dozens of other specialties, PATH develops and scales up innovative solutions to the world’s most pressing health challenges.


PATH’s Center for Vaccine Innovation and Access (CVIA) brings together our expertise across every stage of the long and complex process of vaccine research, development, and delivery to make lifesaving vaccines widely available to children and communities across the world. CVIA’s current portfolio encompasses more than two dozen vaccines either in development or already in use to protect against fifteen different diseases. Our focus is on vaccines to address the leading diseases that claim children’s lives worldwide: pneumonia, diarrheal disease, and malaria; as well as other global health priorities, such as polio and meningitis. We work in partnership with national health ministries, pharmaceutical manufacturers, donors, international financing and regulatory organizations, and many others. PATH has led numerous global partnerships, including the award-winning Meningitis Vaccine Project and the Malaria Vaccine Initiative, which helped develop the first malaria vaccine candidate recommended for pilot implementation.

CVIA seeks a Global Head of Chemistry, Manufacturing and Controls, and Non-clinical Toxicology (Global Head of CMC) to help further our mission to ensure affordable and accessible vaccines for people living in low-income settings. The Global Head of CMC provides leadership and management, operational excellence, and technical expertise to all CMC & NT activities within the CVIA portfolio of vaccine candidates and projects through collaboration with CVIA Project Teams, CVIA Diseases and Functional Areas, and CVIA’s vaccine development partners. This role is also responsible for the assessment of new partnership opportunities with respect to process development, product analytics, manufacturing, and quality control, adherence to WHO Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) and Good Laboratory Practices (GLP) non-clinical safety assessment and toxicity studies of biological products. The CMC team is comprised of approximately 8 CMC experts and also draws on consultants for specialized competencies.

The Global Head of CMC is a member of the CVIA leadership team (CVIA LT) and is responsible for CVIA-wide business plan creation and implementation, change initiative leadership, talent management, and proactive partnership in developing comprehensive cross-disciplinary tactics and enabling exceptional execution through cross-functional collaboration.

Responsibilities:

Chemistry, Manufacturing and Controls (CMC)

  • Functional area-wide leadership and management of Chemistry, Manufacturing and Control, and Non-Clinical Toxicology functional activities, CMC and nonclinical safety assessment and toxicology (NT) functional activities of project team work to ensure on-time and on-budget delivery of CMC & NT-related project objectives and milestones as well as compliance with PATH policies and procedures and international standards (e.g., WHO).
  • Provide strategic and technical guidance to CMC team members on project teams on process development, product analytics, formulation and fill, final manufacturing process and facility design and needs, and quality control thereof, investigational product supply and stability, as well as in vivo and in vitro safety and toxicity testing performed before and during the clinical development to demonstrate non-clinical safety and tolerability of candidate vaccine products.
  • Oversee CMC team preparation and review of reports for partners and donors including project status, risk identification, and potential mitigation strategies.
  • Ensure CMC team support for regulatory submissions such as eCTD Modules 2.3 and 3, by authoring or reviewing CMC content.
  • Interact with partners to provide oversight, guidance, and evaluations of processes in development, laboratories and manufacturing facilities, including process development, product analytics, formulation and fill, manufacturing, and quality control and Validation (Product, Process, Method and Packaging) thereof.
  • Prepare and review quality control guidelines and validation protocols for vaccine process, formulation, product analytical assay development, and in vivo and in vitro safety, toxicity testing and packaging validation.
  • Evaluate industrial processes for robustness, cost efficiency, compliance, quality control, and health/safety/environmental requirements and consider how new tools, such as AI, can be applied.
  • Provide guidance for optimal process and technology transfer from R&D to commercial operations.
  • Perform technical review of CMC plans and technical documentation relative to vaccine manufacturing production, facilities and product analytics, including primary accountability for technical content and quality of regulatory documents submitted by CVIA.
  • Conduct technical due diligence of potential partners and vendors for process development, manufacturing, quality control, and safety and toxicity testing.
  • Review plans against quality control requirements including WHO Prequalification and stringent regulatory authority standards.
  • As needed, serve as CMC lead on more complex project(s) and/or lead CMC technical assistance projects
  • Contribute to partner identification efforts to support product transfer to commercial manufacturers in LMICs.

Management & Leadership

  • Member of the CVIA LT and successfully partnering with other CVIA leaders to support the goals and objectives of vaccine development and introduction.
  • Develop strong partnership with cross-functional peers to ensure overall integrated development and introduction plans and tactics.
  • Ensure resource allocation across vaccine development and introduction projects, technical assistance projects, and change initiatives by providing CMC & NT resources as needed.
  • Develop and enforce functional area norms and standards to ensure quality of CMC & NT technical support on all projects supported by the group.
  • Recruit, supervise, coach, and develop CMC & NT staff.

Required skills and experience:

  • 15+ years of vaccine or biologics industry experience.
  • Ph.D. or master’s in chemistry or vaccine-related field of study.
  • Experience in method, equipment and process validation, and development and validation of product analytics in a cGMP regulated environment.
  • Prefer previous work experience with low-resource setting country manufacturers.
  • Reputation as a flexible team player with the ability to forge consensus in a project-based matrix organization and align with other vaccine development and introduction leaders.
  • Demonstrated senior management level capacity to manage diverse and varied job responsibilities.
  • Excellent written (especially technical writing), verbal and interpersonal communication skills.
  • Ability and willingness to travel domestically and internationally, up to 25% annually.
  • Must have legal authorization to work in PATH country office location.

PATH is a diverse nonprofit organization that creates a culture of collaboration and partnership. Learn more about the impact you can make globally here.

We offer our employees a competitive salary and generous benefits. For candidates based in the U.S., the annual salary range for this position is $320,000-$380,000. The final salary is based on a variety of objective factors. PATH provides a comprehensive benefit package that includes 15 vacation, 11 holiday, 2 personal, and 12 sick days per year; medical and dental plans; life insurance; and disability and retirement benefits. For more details click here.

Remote & Hybrid Work

PATH operates within a hybrid workplace model unless otherwise noted. Hybrid employees reside within commuting distance of one of our PATH offices. PATH’s US offices are located in Seattle, WA, and Washington, DC. This position is approved to be a remote employee from a US state where PATH is registered.

Manager of Ocean Transportation

About the Position

Luminary Logistics Solutions is seeking an experienced and proactive Manager of Ocean Transportation to coordinate and manage international ocean freight processes from customer award through final delivery.

This is a hands-on operational position focused on managing shipments, coordinating documentation, maintaining communication with Project Managers and transportation partners, and ensuring ocean freight movements are completed efficiently and on schedule.

The ideal candidate is highly organized, detail-oriented, and capable of independently managing ocean transportation activities without direct supervision. This position does not include employee management responsibilities.

Key Responsibilities

    Ocean Freight Operations

    • Take ownership of ocean transportation processes from customer award through shipment execution and final delivery.
    • Coordinate FCL, LCL, breakbulk, out-of-gauge, and specialized ocean cargo shipments.
    • Arrange ocean freight bookings and coordinate vessel schedules, cargo readiness, and shipping deadlines.
    • Monitor ocean shipments and proactively address delays, documentation issues, and operational challenges.
    • Coordinate with ocean carriers, freight agents, terminals, customs brokers, and other transportation partners.
    • Ensure transportation activities comply with applicable shipping regulations and company procedures.

      • Documentation & Process Management

      • Become involved in ocean transportation requirements immediately following customer award.
      • Receive, review, and coordinate ocean shipping documentation.
      • Proactively follow up with Project Managers when required documentation or shipment information is missing.
      • Prepare, review, and coordinate bills of lading, shipping instructions, packing lists, and other required documents.
      • Track documentation deadlines, vessel cutoffs, and shipment milestones.
      • Maintain accurate records and shipment information within company operating systems.
      • Identify opportunities to improve documentation workflows and operational processes.

        • Project Coordination & Operations Support

        • Work closely with Project Managers to ensure ocean transportation requirements are addressed throughout each project.
        • Provide ocean freight expertise and operational guidance to internal teams.
        • Coordinate shipment timelines and communicate changes affecting project execution.
        • Serve as a secondary operational resource, assisting with other freight forwarding activities when needed.
        • Maintain proactive communication with Operations, Sourcing, and other departments.
        • Ensure assigned responsibilities are completed accurately and within established deadlines.

          • Cost Control & Risk Management

          • Obtain and review ocean freight rates, carrier quotations, and transportation-related charges.
          • Monitor shipment costs and identify potential financial risks.
          • Proactively address potential demurrage, detention, storage, and other avoidable transportation expenses.
          • Communicate shipment delays, missed deadlines, and potential cost exposure to Project Managers and leadership.
          • Assist in resolving carrier invoice discrepancies and transportation-related billing issues.

            • Communication & Customer Service

            • Maintain timely communication with internal stakeholders, carriers, vendors, and customers as appropriate.
            • Provide accurate updates regarding vessel schedules, shipment progress, and documentation requirements.
            • Respond promptly to operational requests and shipping-related questions.
            • Demonstrate ownership, accountability, and effective problem-solving throughout the shipment process.

Required Qualifications

    • Minimum of 5 years of experience in international ocean freight forwarding or ocean transportation operations.
    • Strong understanding of ocean freight booking procedures, documentation, and shipping requirements.
    • Experience coordinating ocean import and/or export shipments.
    • Knowledge of vessel schedules, port operations, and international shipping deadlines.
    • Experience working with ocean carriers, freight agents, and Project Managers.
    • Ability to independently manage multiple shipments and competing deadlines.
    • Strong attention to detail and organizational skills.
    • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
    • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and freight forwarding or transportation management systems.
    • Ability to work independently in a remote environment.

Preferred Qualifications

    • Experience with project cargo, breakbulk, heavy-lift, or oversized shipments.
    • Experience using CargoWise or similar freight forwarding software.
    • Knowledge of Incoterms and international trade documentation.
    • Experience coordinating customs clearance and working with international freight agents.
    • Familiarity with freight cost management and carrier rate negotiations.

What We're Looking For

    We are seeking someone who is proactive, dependable, and comfortable taking ownership of ocean freight processes from beginning to end.
    The successful candidate will anticipate operational challenges, follow up on missing information without being prompted, communicate effectively, and ensure shipments move forward according to established timelines.
    This role is ideal for an experienced ocean freight professional who enjoys hands-on operational work, process coordination, and problem-solving rather than employee supervision.

About Sellers Dorsey

Sellers Dorsey is a healthcare impact strategy firm focused on improving care access, quality, and outcomes for our nation’s most vulnerable populations. We work with providers, managed care organizations, state entities, and others, to design, implement, fund, and optimize sustainable programs that deliver maximum impact to underserved communities. Built on decades of experience in Medicaid, our team includes former state Medicaid directors, healthcare policy experts, health plan execs, and hospital leaders who know how to navigate the complexities of the system and find creative, impactful solutions that drive the greatest impact for the individuals and communities that need it most.

About the Role

Sellers Dorsey is seeking a Research Analyst (Healthcare Finance Sales) who will support the Sales team in the firm's National Medicaid Financing practice. As the Research Analyst, you will research hospitals, physicians, and state Medicaid environments and turn that research into reports that help sales staff and leadership decide which Medicaid financing opportunities to pursue and which prospective clients could benefit from the firm's work on enhanced Medicaid funding initiatives. Those initiatives help providers improve access, quality, and equity in healthcare.

This role is highly visible, produces research for senior leadership with little supervision, and works across functions to keep every output accurate. It also offers a direct path to build deep Medicaid policy, financing, and technical expertise, and its scope can grow over time based on the individual's skills and interests.

Key Responsibilities

  • Research & Analysis: Research and analyze Medicaid financing programs and provider financial data from multiple sources, including cost reports and state budget information. Build profiles of hospitals, physicians, and state environments that show where Medicaid financing opportunities exist.

  • Sales Team Reporting: Create usable custom reports for Sales team staff and leadership to guide prospect identification and pursuit. Work with colleagues across functions to confirm that reports are technically accurate and delivered on time.

  • Research Standards:Establish and maintain standards for research work products, including research procedures and templates.

Key Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Health policy, health care finance, health administration, or a related discipline is required. Advanced degree in a relevant healthcare program, such as public health (MPH) or health administration (MHA) is preferred, or advanced degree in analytics, finance, business, or economics, combined with relevant healthcare experience.

  • 3-4 years of professional experience in Medicaid, health care, and/or human services, or 1-2 years of experience combined with relevant advanced education. An exceptional candidate with relevant advanced education and no professional experience may be considered.

  • Strong math and Excel skills. These are required alongside healthcare experience, not in place of it.

  • Experience developing research work products independently for senior leadership.

  • Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook). Advanced Excel to import, organize, and analyze large data sets is essential.

  • Familiarity with financial modeling, or the ability to learn it quickly.

  • SharePoint and other Microsoft products are useful.

Additional Experience (Preferred)

  • Finance analysis experience.

  • Knowledge of the state health care landscape: Medicaid, state health and human services agencies, public health, health insurance, or managed care.

  • Background in an academic program or other accelerated learning environment involving health care research and intelligence.

Other Requirements

  • Self-starter who manages ambiguous tasks and objectives and uses sound judgment to solve problems.

  • Quantitative and qualitative research skills, with strong analytical and organizational skills.

  • Ability to locate, evaluate, and synthesize public information on Medicaid and other healthcare programs, such as cost reports and state budget information on Medicaid providers.

  • Clear written and oral communication, including concise summaries of technical material and internal work products.

  • Ability to manage complex projects autonomously. Project management skills, both receiving and leading direction (time management, task delegation, PM tools).

  • Ability to communicate across functions to close knowledge gaps and keep work accurate and timely.

  • Works independently and in teams. Interacts professionally with colleagues and clients and coordinates the work of others as needed.

Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States. Sellers Dorsey does not sponsor employment visas at this time. Employment with Sellers Dorsey is contingent upon successful completion of a background check.

Compensation & Benefits

The anticipated salary range for candidates is $65,400/year in our lowest geographic market range to up to $90,000/year. The final pay offered to a successful candidate will be dependent on several factors that may include but are not limited to the type and years of experience within the job, the type of years and experience within the industry, the candidate’s education, and the candidate’s market location. Typically, candidates are not hired near the top of the range and compensation decisions are made based upon Sellers Dorsey’s Total Compensation Policies & Guidelines. The successful candidate will also be eligible to participate in our annual Corporate Incentive Plan (CIP) that can range to up to 7% of annual salary.

Provided they meet all eligibility requirements under the applicable plan documents, the successful candidate (and their eligible dependents) will be eligible to enroll in group healthcare plans that offer medical, dental, and vision and for insurance plans offering short term disability, long term disability, and basic life. Employees are also able to enroll in Sellers Dorsey’s 401k plan provided they meet plan requirements. Sellers Dorsey offers a Flexible Time Off that allows employees to use what they need. Additionally, we offer 10 paid holidays throughout the calendar year, paid time off for qualifying medical leave, and up to 12 weeks of combined paid parental and bonding leave. The foregoing benefits and paid time off, including an employee’s eligibility therefore, will be controlled by applicable plan documents and Sellers Dorsey policy.

Description

Earnix is seeking a Creative Director to lead the creative vision for the brand and the production that brings it to life. Reporting to the Head of Brand, Creative & Communications, you will own the story we tell and the creative direction behind it. You will bring a digital and video first mindset to everything we make, with an overarching focus on bringing the brand to life in innovative ways across every channel and touchpoint.

This is a leadership role that pairs big-idea creative leadership with deep production expertise. You will develop the ideas that anchor our campaigns, set the standard for creative quality and innovation, and take ownership of how the work is produced, from video content to large-scale event experiences.

You will direct the agencies, production companies and creative partners who deliver the work, and collaborate closely with marketing, product, sales and executive leadership to ensure our creative strategy supports the company’s business objectives. We deliver a great deal with focused resources, so you will bring a resourceful, hands-on approach and find efficient ways to deliver high-impact work.

What You’ll Do

Own the big idea. Develop and steward the overarching creative concepts and narrative that bring our brand and strategy to life, and make them hold together across campaigns, products and regions.

Set creative direction across the organization. Provide the vision and guardrails for marketing materials across brand, demand generation, product marketing, sales enablement, digital and corporate communications.

Lead with digital. Set the creative approach for web, social and owned channels, building ideas digital first and extending them into video, events and experiential so the brand feels connected everywhere it appears.

Lead production end to end. Oversee production from concept to delivery across video, events and experiential, including scripting, budgets, schedules, vendors and post-production, ensuring work is delivered on time, on budget and to a high standard of craft.

Own video. Champion video as a core storytelling medium and oversee its production, from brand videos and launch content to product storytelling, customer stories and social-first formats, directing writers, production and editors.

Run event and experiential production. Direct the creative and production for events and experiential: keynote and stage experiences, booths and venue environments, signage, and on-site moments, working with event partners and venues to deliver on site.

Push innovation in execution. Explore new formats, technologies and approaches, including AI-enabled creative and emerging digital platforms, and apply them where they sharpen the idea rather than for novelty.

Manage creative and production partners. Select, brief and direct agencies, production companies, freelancers and event partners. Give clear, inspiring direction and sharp feedback, and keep work on brief, on budget and on brand.

Guard and evolve the brand. Keep the brand system, voice and visual identity consistent while letting it grow, and align creative with brand strategy, positioning and messaging.

Collaborate and influence. Partner closely with marketing, product, sales, communications and executive leadership, presenting concepts and building buy-in at senior levels.

Develop standards and capability. Raise the creative bar and establish production standards, workflows and best practices for the team and the wider organization through clear principles and feedback.

Requirements

What We're Looking For

10-15 years of creative experience, including significant time as a Creative Director, Head of Production or in an equivalent leadership role.

Proven experience running production at scale, with hands-on command of video production from concept through post-production and of live event or experiential production, including budgets, schedules, and vendors.

A resourceful, hands-on approach to delivering high-impact work

jobs.excerpt: Brilliant is seeking a full-time Associate Director, Client Management for our Influencer & Celebrity team.
jobs.description:
Brilliant is seeking a full-time Associate Director, Client Management for our Influencer & Celebrity team. This role will own the day-to-day client relationship and keep every influencer program on time, on budget, and flawlessly executed.

The Role

This is a client-facing, project-management-first role. All day, every day, you are the voice of Brilliant to our clients: you run the calls, write the recap, chase the approvals, and make sure nothing slips. Our strategy and talent leads build the programs; you make sure they get delivered.

You are hyper-organized. You know where every creator, contract, deliverable, and invoice stands at any moment. You understand influencer budgets inside and out, and you have done this in high-volume agency settings where dozens of creators and multiple brands are live at once.

Who We Are

We’re a fully remote performance team built on a simple promise: Work Hard. Play Hard. Laugh Hard.

We aren't for the faint of heart. We move fast, hold a ridiculously high bar for excellence, and thrive on driving real ROI for our clients. But we also believe that intense drive should come with great culture, which is why we offer unlimited PTO, Fabulous Fridays (doors close at 3pm), virtual happy hours, a monthly book club, and endless reasons to win together.

And the industry notices: we were recently named an Inc. Best Workplace 2026 and landed on the Inc. 5000 List of America's Fastest-Growing Private Companies for 2026.

What We Do

Since 2008, Brilliant has been where bold ideas meet relentless execution. We're a performance marketing agency with deep expertise in family-focused brands, bringing together PR, Influencer, Social, Paid Media, Affiliate, Retail Support, Experiential, and AI Intelligence to create integrated, full-funnel campaigns that shatter targets and cut through the noise.

What You'll Do

Own the client relationship

  • Serve as the primary day-to-day point of contact for multiple influencer and celebrity accounts across Zoom, email, and Slack.
  • Lead weekly status calls and client meetings, and send same-day recaps with clear next steps, owners, and deadlines.
  • Know your clients’ brands, products, retail calendars, and stakeholders cold, and build relationships they trust.
  • Manage expectations proactively: flag risks early, present solutions, and keep clients informed before they have to ask.
  • Pull together campaign data, content, and results for client reviews, QBRs, and milestone presentations.
  • Listen critically in every meeting to spot incremental opportunities within existing accounts, and bring them to leadership.

Run the project, end to end

  • Own campaign timelines from kickoff through final reporting, so every program is delivered on time and aligned with client objectives.
  • Build and maintain project management tools and trackers (AirTable, Asana, or similar) that give the team and clients a single source of truth.
  • Track every moving piece: creator outreach, contracts, product shipments, content drafts, client approvals, go-live dates, and usage windows.
  • Coordinate across Brilliant’s strategy, talent, paid media, PR, social, and analytics teams to keep integrated campaigns in sync.
  • Ensure every program meets FTC disclosure guidelines and brand safety standards.
  • Keep creator issues to a minimum, and handle the ones that arise calmly and quickly.

Manage the money

  • Own influencer budgets on assigned accounts: track talent spend, gifting, product costs, fees, and paid amplification against approved budgets.
  • Build and maintain budget trackers and flag overages or underspend before they become problems.
  • Lead monthly billing reconciliation with finance, making sure creator payments, invoices, and client billing match.
  • Provide inputs on account profitability and scope, and raise when work is drifting out of scope.

Lead and develop the team

  • Oversee specialists and coordinators on campaign execution, and set the standard for client correspondence, follow-through, and attention to detail.
  • Mentor junior team members: what training do they need, and how can we encourage their growth?
  • Help build and improve the client management processes, templates, and playbooks that let the team scale without sacrificing quality.

Stay sharp

  • Keep a pulse on TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, Facebook, Pinterest, and emerging platforms, and share trends with clients and the team.
  • Bring energy to brainstorms and push the team to think bigger.

Our Dream Team Member

  • 5–7 years of client service or account management experience, with at least 3 years in influencer marketing.
  • Experience in a high-volume influencer agency setting, managing many creators and multiple brands at once. Large-agency experience strongly preferred.
  • A deep understanding of influencer budgets: talent rates, fees, gifting, usage rights, whitelisting costs, and how they roll up to a client budget.
  • Experience leading monthly billing reconciliation and tracking account profitability.
  • Hyper-organized. You build the tracker, you live in the tracker, and you never miss a deadline.
  • Fluency in project management tools such as AirTable or Asana, plus familiarity with CreatorIQ, HypeAuditor, Shopify Collabs, or similar platforms.
  • Working knowledge of paid, gifted, affiliate, and ambassador programs, plus whitelisting, Spark Ads, and Partnership Ads.
  • Experience overseeing or mentoring junior team members.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, with composure and confidence on camera in client meetings.
  • Can manage up, manage down, and keep a million moving pieces running smoothly.
  • Resourceful, committed, deliberate, and genuinely enjoys crossing things off the list.

Bonus Points

  • Experience with parenting, baby, kids, toy, or family lifestyle brands.
  • Experience with celebrity talent partnerships and working with agents, managers, and publicists.
  • Experience on integrated campaigns that combine influencer with PR, experiential, or retail activations.
  • A slight obsession with Amazon, online shopping, and discovering new products.

Benefits

  • Unlimited PTO
  • Paid time off between Christmas and New Year's
  • Fabulous Fridays: the work day ends at 3pm all year
  • 401K with a 3% company match (immediately vested) after the initial 3 months
  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • Medical and Dependent Care FSA
  • Company-paid Life Insurance
  • Company-paid Long-Term Disability
