jobs.description:
Job Title: Local Study Project Manager - Sponsor dedicated

Job Location: London, Greater London, United Kingdom

Job Location Type: Remote

Job Contract Type: Full-time

Job Seniority Level:

The Local Study Project Manager leads Local Study Teams at country level to deliver committed components of clinical studies according to agreed resources, budget and timelines complying with IQVIA or Sponsor Procedural Documents and International guidelines such as ICF-GCP as well as relevant local regulations.

Responsible to ensure the sites are identified, site qualifications performed, set up, initiated, monitored, closed and documentation archived, to ensure site activation, initiation and maintenance of regulatory activities for selected studies, to perform oversight of local regulatory and ethics submission packages, to oversee milestones planning and strategy for study submission, to oversee the study budget.

Main Responsibilities


  • Leads Local Study Team consisting of CRAs and Study Start Up Specialists for assigned studies. Ensures, as required, the clinical and operational feasibility assessment of potential studies is performed to the highest quality.
  • Coordinates the site selection process with relevant stakeholders.
  • Plans and coordinates applicable local drug activities (from local purchase or reimbursement to drug destruction).
  • Sets up and maintains the study in applicable systems at study country level as well as local websites as required by local laws and regulations.
  • Oversees, manages and coordinates monitoring activities from site activation through to study closure at country and site level in accordance with the Monitoring Plan.
  • Proactively identifies risks and facilitates resolution of complex study problems and issues.
  • Organizes regular Local Study Team meetings on an agenda driven basis.
  • Reports study progress/update to the Global Study Associate Director/Global Study Team.
  • Assists in forecasting study timelines, resources, recruitment, budget, study materials and drug supplies.
  • Ensures relevant systems required to facilitate business critical, license to operate activities (for example, Regulatory Submissions) are set-up, updated and access is organized at country level.
  • Ensures accurate payments related to the study are performed according to local regulations and agreements.
  • Participates in training and coaching new members of the Local Study Team ensuring compliance with ICG-GCP and IQVIA or Sponsor Procedural Documents.
  • Ensures completeness of the applicable TMF system and ensures essential documents are uploaded in a timely manner to maintain “Inspection Ready” status of applicable systems.
  • Plans and leads activities associated with audits and regulatory inspections in liaison with Quality Assurance.
  • Oversees the execution of Site Activation and/or Maintenance for assigned studies in accordance with the agreed Start Up strategy, adhering to project timelines.
  • Ensures collaboration across Regulatory and Start Up & Site Activation, including communication with regions and countries, to successfully deliver the agreed project scope.
  • Provides specialist regulatory and technical scientific support to Start Up team.
  • Determines regulatory strategy/expectations and parameters for submissions and all necessary authorizations.
  • Assesses and reviews the regulatory landscape and contributes to the collection, interpretation, analysis and dissemination of accurate regulatory intelligence to support assigned studies.
  • Ensures accurate completion and maintenance of internal systems, databases, tracking tools, timelines and project plans with project specific information.

Required Skills and Qualifications


  • Bachelor's Degree Life sciences or related field.
  • 7 years’ relevant experience in a scientific or clinical environment. Equivalent combination of education, training and experience.
  • Knowledge of Oncology therapeutical area.
  • Proven work experience in Phase III studies.
  • Strong negotiation and communication skills with ability to challenge.
  • Excellent interpersonal skills and strong team player.
  • Proven ability to work through others to deliver results to the appropriate quality and timeline metrics on complex projects.
  • Thorough understanding of regulated clinical trial environment and in-depth knowledge of drug development process, including site monitoring experience.
  • Demonstrated proficiency in using systems and technology to achieve work objectives.
  • Good regulatory and technical writing skills.
  • Strong knowledge and ability to apply Clinical Practice (GCP) and International Conference on Harmonization (ICH) guidelines and applicable regulatory guidelines.
  • Excellent understanding of study financial management.
  • Proven ability to work on multiple projects balancing competing priorities.
  • Very good knowledge of English language.

• Willingness to travel occasionally.

Please note: due to sponsor requirements for the role only candidates based in the listed location/s will be considered. Any applications from candidates based outside of these locations will not be considered.

*Please note this role is not eligible for UK visa sponsorship.

What You'll Do:

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Support program startup, organizational design, implementation planning, and change management for new grants and allocations.

  • Mentor policy specialists and coordinate work across legal, environmental, financial, construction, housing, technology, and compliance functions.

  • Support proposals, client presentations, capture strategy, and thought leadership related to disaster recovery and community development.

  • Perform other duties of a similar nature and level as assigned to meet project, client, and organizational needs.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in public administration, planning, public policy, law, business, housing, or a related field.

  • At least ten years of grants, housing, community development, or public-sector program experience, including seven years in CDBG-DR, CDBG-MIT, or comparable HUD disaster recovery work.

jobs.description:
AIRS Medical is a healthcare technology company using AI to make medical imaging faster and more accessible. Our FDA-cleared solution, SwiftMR, accelerates MRI scans by up to 50%, helping healthcare providers improve efficiency and the patient experience. As we continue to grow, we’re looking for people who want to make a meaningful impact on the future of healthcare.

🔹 AIRS Commercial Philosophy

At AIRS, we believe disciplined thinking and strong commercial results reinforce one another.

We expect our people to meet or exceed their commitments, create pipeline proactively, forecast accurately, and deliver consistent performance. How we achieve those results matters: through sound judgment, strong discovery, credible business cases, executive engagement, and helping clients make good decisions.

Our job is not to convince every client to buy AIRS. It is to understand what the client is trying to accomplish, determine whether there is a problem worth solving, quantify why it matters, and help the organization make a sound decision.

We value discernment over persuasion, evidence over assumption, and meaningful progress over activity alone.

Our commercial team operates within a disciplined model for account strategy, discovery, qualification, business-case development, executive engagement, and opportunity management. We value process because it improves judgment and execution, while still expecting independent thinking, adaptability, and sound commercial instincts.

Across every role, we look for people who are curious, coachable, commercially minded, comfortable with ambiguity, capable of thinking on their feet, and accountable for measurable outcomes.

🔹 The Opportunity

The Market Executive owns commercial performance across a defined geographic market and account universe.

This role is for a seller who can create demand, understand the local market, develop relationships, diagnose problems, build credible business cases, and close business without waiting for opportunities to be handed to them.

You are expected to know your market, create opportunity within it, and act as the commercial quarterback for AIRS across the accounts you own.

Requirements

🔹 What You Will Own

  • Revenue and pipeline within your market
  • New account development
  • Existing client expansion
  • Market and account strategy
  • Prospecting and opportunity creation
  • Discovery and qualification
  • Business-case development
  • Opportunity progression and close
  • Local execution within strategic accounts where appropriate
  • Forecast accuracy and CRM discipline

🔹 Results You Will Deliver

  • Meet or exceed annual revenue quota
  • Consistently create enough qualified pipeline to support future attainment
  • Win new clients and expand existing relationships
  • Maintain accurate forecasts and opportunity data
  • Progress opportunities through the AIRS sales process with discipline
  • Deliver consistent quarterly performance rather than relying on isolated large wins
  • Increase penetration across your assigned market
  • Convert meaningful client problems into well-qualified commercial opportunities

🔹 What Great Looks Like

You consistently create opportunity rather than depend on inbound demand.

You understand enough about the client’s business to move comfortably between radiology, operations, finance, technology, and executive stakeholders.

You do not rush to demonstrate product capability before understanding what matters.

You know how to determine whether an opportunity is real, what remains unknown, who matters, what needs to happen next, and whether continued investment of time is warranted.

🔹 What You Will Do

  • Develop and execute a market strategy
  • Prospect strategically across assigned accounts
  • Build relationships with clinical, operational, technical, financial, and executive stakeholders
  • Conduct high-quality discovery
  • Identify and quantify operational and economic impact
  • Develop client-specific business cases
  • Build and execute account and opportunity plans
  • Manage complex opportunities from initial engagement through contract
  • Coordinate with Commercial Development Representatives, Directors of Strategic Accounts, Clinical, Marketing, Product, and client Success
  • Maintain accurate pipeline and forecast visibility
  • Use the AIRS operating model consistently while exercising independent judgment

🔹 The Athlete We Are Looking For

You are:

  • Curious and commercially minded
  • Strong at asking questions and listening for what matters
  • Comfortable creating your own opportunities
  • Able to think on your feet
  • Financially fluent enough to discuss ROI, capacity, revenue, capital, and operating impact
  • Coachable and actively interested in improving your craft
  • Organized without being rigid
  • Competitive without becoming transactional
  • Comfortable changing your point of view when the evidence changes
  • Able to prosecute an opportunity with discipline from discovery through close
  • Comfortable helping a client reach a decision, even when the answer may not immediately favor AIRS
  • Accountable for consistent production, not simply occasional wins

🔹 What You Bring

Required

  • Successful B2B selling experience
  • Demonstrated ability to generate pipeline and close business
  • Experience navigating multi-stakeholder sales cycles
  • Strong communication, business acumen, and judgment
  • Evidence of coachability and learning agility
  • Track record of meeting or exceeding quota

Preferred

  • Healthcare, medtech, enterprise technology, or medical imaging experience
  • Experience selling business value rather than product features
  • Experience selling to hospitals, imaging centers, or physician-led organizations

Benefits

🔹 What AIRS Offers

  • The chance to help build the commercial organization, not just step into a finished one
  • Real ownership and visibility, with direct access to senior leadership
  • A product with clear clinical and economic value in a large, underpenetrated market
  • A high-performance environment that rewards judgment, curiosity, accountability, and results
  • Exposure to complex customer problems and some of the largest health systems and imaging organizations in the country
  • Meaningful opportunity to grow as the company scales
  • Competitive compensation, benefits, and equity

Our culture and our people are special. We’re looking for people who are – or want to become – part of the communities where clients live, work and worship. About the Role

The Strategic Project Lead – Multimodal AI supports frontier AI development through complex, high-quality data programs for leading AI companies. We’re looking for someone with experience in multimodal AI data, such as image, video, 3D, sensor, or robotics-related workflows.

You’ll lead projects that turn complex real-world data into reliable training and evaluation resources. Combining project management with hands-on domain knowledge, you’ll partner with clients and internal teams to design workflows, maintain quality, and solve challenging data delivery problems in a rapidly evolving AI market.

Your Impact

  • Own end-to-end project delivery across scope, timelines, budgets, staffing, and risks.
  • Lead client communication, status reporting, planning sessions, and escalations.
  • Translate technical and client requirements into data collection workflows, annotation guidelines, tooling, and quality standards.
  • Define quality metrics and acceptance criteria for multimodal data and annotation outputs.
  • Monitor delivery quality, troubleshoot data issues, and resolve ambiguous requirements with clients.
  • Advise on project feasibility, collection methods, annotation approaches, and tooling based on your domain expertise.
  • Build reusable SOPs, guidelines, and QA frameworks to support consistent delivery.
  • Mentor Operations Specialists and contribute to project scoping, pilots, and emerging multimodal AI capabilities.

What You Bring

  • 1–2+ years of experience in AI data operations, project coordination, or delivery, ideally in a GenAI or frontier AI environment.
  • Familiarity with at least one multimodal data workflow involving images, video, 3D data, sensors, or robotics.
  • Experience coordinating projects or workstreams, managing stakeholders, and communicating with clients.
  • Understanding of data quality, annotation workflows, and quality assurance methods.
  • Ability to translate project requirements into clear data collection workflows, annotation guidelines, and quality standards.
  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-moving environment.
  • Interest in current AI developments, including multimodal models, spatial AI, or embodied AI.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with image or video annotation, 3D data, point clouds, or sensor data.
  • Familiarity with robotics data collection or real-world perception workflows.
  • Exposure to 2D or 3D labeling, segmentation, tracking, or structured annotation tasks.
  • Experience with autonomous systems, spatial AI, or embodied AI.
  • Bilingual capabilities, particularly German or a Nordic language.

Why You'll Love Working Here

    At Appen, we foster a culture of innovation, collaboration, and excellence. We value curiosity, accountability, and a commitment to delivering the highest quality AI solutions for frontier models.

    You'll work on complex challenges that shape the future of AI across industries and geographies, alongside talented people in a culture that values humility over ego. You'll have the flexibility to deliver in a way that works for you and your team, supported by tools, resources, and development opportunities to continue to build your capability over time.

About Appen

    Appen has been a leader in AI training data for over 30 years. We specialise in human generated data to train, fine tune, and evaluate models across generative AI, large language models, computer vision, and speech recognition. Our AI assisted data annotation platform and global crowd of more than 1 million contributors in over 200 countries support model pre training, supervised fine tuning, evaluation and benchmarking, safety and red teaming, and multilingual global expansion.

jobs.title: Director of Demand and Inventory Planning
jobs.excerpt: Real people.  Real service. At SupplyHouse. com, we value every individual team member and cultivate a community where people come first.
jobs.description:
Real people. Real service.

At SupplyHouse.com, we value every individual team member and cultivate a community where people come first. Led by our core values of Generosity, Respect, Innovation, Teamwork, and GRIT, we’re dedicated to maintaining a supportive work environment that celebrates diversity and empowers everyone to reach their full potential. As an industry-leading e-commerce company specializing in HVAC, plumbing, heating, and electrical supplies since 2004, we strive to foster growth while providing the best possible experience for our customers.

We are looking for a Director of Demand and Inventory Planning to join our Operations Team! This individual will report into our Senior Vice President, Fulfillment Operations and lead our end-to-end inventory planning function, overseeing demand forecasting, replenishment, and inventory allocation across our fulfillment network. This role will be responsible for optimizing inventory investments to maintain product availability, improve inventory turnover, and drive profitability. Working closely with partners across Merchandising, Finance, Supply Chain Operations, and executive leadership, this individual will align demand and inventory strategies with broader business and financial objectives. If you’re passionate about inventory optimization, enjoy using data to drive strategic decisions, and are excited to lead initiatives that improve operational efficiency and support business growth, we’d love to hear from you!

This remote position is open to individuals who live in, or are open to relocating to, the following states: Arizona, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, Nevada, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Rhode Island, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Virginia, and Washington.

This position requires approximately 20% travel, including visits to our fulfillment centers and travel to our headquarters in Melville, NY 6 times per year for internal meetings and team-building activities. We reimburse reasonable and necessary travel expenses, and you’re also welcome to work on-site anytime beyond these visits – our doors are always open.

Role Type: Full-Time, Exempt

Location: Remote

Schedule: Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. with time zone flexibility

Base Salary: The expected starting salary for the position is $189,175 to $270,250 within a full position range of $189,175 to $351,325 annually. This range reflects the long-term earning potential for the role. Our starting pay practice is the minimum to middle portion of the range, depending on experience, qualifications, and internal equity, consistent with applicable law and it is rare for a new hire to start above the midpoint.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Inventory strategy and governance
    • Define and lead our inventory strategy, including SKU segmentation, service level targets, and stocking policy by fulfillment center
    • Establish clear guardrails that balance service, working capital, and profitability, with defined decision rights across functions
    • Build the framework for SKU governance, including how new items are introduced and how unproductive inventory is identified and exited
    • Define the criteria for which SKUs we own and stock versus which are better served through marketplace or third-party fulfillment, balancing customer speed and experience, margin, and inventory investment
    • Own the long-term inventory planning roadmap across process, systems, and operating model
  • Demand forecasting
    • Establish an enterprise forecasting framework with clear accuracy measures and accountability
    • Combine historical data, system-driven forecasting, and merchant input into a single, SKU-level demand signal
    • Account for seasonality, promotions, product lifecycle, and regional demand patterns
  • Replenishment and network allocation
    • Own replenishment execution, including purchase order quantities, across all categories
    • Determine where inventory should be positioned across our fulfillment centers to maximize same-day and next-day delivery reach while managing total inventory investment
    • Improve lead time accuracy and vendor performance in partnership with Merchandising and vendor partners
  • Performance and KPI ownership
    • Establish and own inventory KPIs, including in-stock and fill rate, forecast accuracy, inventory turns and weeks of supply, GMROI, and overall inventory productivity
    • Deliver clear executive reporting with root-cause analysis and corrective action
  • Cross-functional leadership
    • Serve as the primary inventory planning partner to Merchandising, Finance, and Supply Chain Operations. Merchandising owns category financial plans, assortment, and margin strategy; you own translating those plans into inventory decisions
    • Partner with Finance on annual budgeting, ongoing reforecasting, and inventory investment targets
  • Systems, data, and operating model
    • Own planning systems strategy and adoption, and work with IT, Analytics, and our automation and WMS programs to build the reporting and forecasting tools the team needs
  • Leadership and talent development
    • Build, develop, and retain a high-performing planning organization
    • Assess the current team structure and design the model that fits our growth, including whether forecasting and replenishment should be organized as separate functions
    • Develop bench strength and succession plans, and foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

What you will bring:

  • Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Business, Finance, Operations, or a related field (MBA preferred)
  • 10+ years of progressive experience in demand planning, inventory planning, or supply chain
  • 4+ years of experience leading professional-level teams
  • Proven success improving inventory productivity, service levels, and working capital
  • Strong financial acumen and experience managing inventory investment
  • Experience in e-commerce, wholesale distribution, and multi-site distribution environments
  • Experience managing inventory decisions in a model that blends owned inventory with marketplace or drop-ship assortment
  • Experience with forecasting, replenishment, ERP, and planning systems, and with S&OP processes including machine learning and AI capabilities
  • Advanced analytical skills and the ability to influence senior stakeholders

Why work with us:

  • We have awesome benefits – We offer a wide variety of benefits to help support you and your loved ones. These include:
    • Comprehensive and affordable medical, dental, vision, and voluntary life insurance options
    • 401(k) with up to 4% company match
    • Paid vacation, sick time, and holidays
    • Company-paid basic life insurance and long-term disability
    • Discounted auto, home, and pet insurance programs
    • Flexible Spending Account (FSA)
    • Confidential mental health, financial planning, and legal support through our Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
    • Company-provided equipment and one-time $250 work from home stipend
    • $750 annual professional development budget
    • $25 monthly Grubhub credit
    • Company rewards and recognition program
    • And more!
  • We empower ownership –We all contribute to our success and we all share in it. Our Ownership for All program ensures each SupplyHouse team member will benefit financially from the company’s growth and accomplishments.
  • We promote work-life balance –We value your time and encourage a healthy separation between your professional and personal life to feel refreshed and recharged. Look out for our wellness initiatives and ask about our Flex-Time Policy!
  • We support growth –We encourage you to embrace continuous learning and take on new challenges. In an exciting and evolving industry, we provide opportunities for career growth through our annual merit and bonus opportunities, hands-on training, diversity and inclusion initiatives, internal mobility options, and professional development budget.
  • We give back – We live and breathe our core value, Generosity, by giving back to the trades and organizations around the world. We make a difference through donation drives, employee-nominated contributions, support for non-profit organizations, Volunteer Paid Time Off, and more.
  • We listen – We value hearing from our employees. Everyone has a voice, and we encourage you to use it! We actively elicit feedback through our monthly town halls, regular 1:1 check-ins, employee listening initiatives, and company-wide ideas form to incorporate suggestions and ensure our team enjoys coming to work every day.

Check us out and learn more at: !

Additional Details:

  • Remote employees are expected to work in a distraction-free environment. Personal devices, background noise, and other distractions should be kept to a minimum to avoid disrupting virtual meetings or business operations.
  • Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the U.S. on a full-time basis. SupplyHouse.com will not sponsor applicants for work visas.
  • SupplyHouse.com is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We welcome and encourage individuals of all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives to apply. Employment decisions are based on qualifications, merit, and business needs.
  • To ensure fairness and trust in our hiring process, we ask that all application materials, assessments, and interview responses reflect your own thinking and perspective. You may use AI tools to assist in preparing your responses, as long as this use is clearly disclosed and you can speak authentically to your ideas and work. Our focus is on honesty, judgment, and how you approach problem-solving. We appreciate your transparency and look forward to learning more about your skills.
  • We are committed to providing a safe and secure work environment and conduct thorough background checks on all potential employees in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.
  • All emails from the SupplyHouse team will only be sent from an @supplyhouse.com email address. Please exercise caution if you receive an email from an alternate domain.

jobs.description:
Job Description: Creative Strategist

Role summary

YAMU Media is hiring a Creative Strategist to own the creative side of paid media for a pod of 5 to 8 clients. You decide what gets made, write and direct it, and use what the ads do in market to decide what gets made next.

This is a hands-on role. You write the scripts (using AI to draft at volume, then editing by hand), find and brief the talent, give direction on raw footage, and guide the editors and designers. You also read the performance data yourself and set the priority list for new creative, so the work stays tied to results.

What you'll own

  • Write scripts. Turn the creative angle, customer research and past winners into hooks and full video scripts for each client. Write every hook, re-hook and call to action, and make each script easy for talent to deliver and easy for an editor to cut.
  • Source talent. Find, vet and book the creators and on-camera talent each client needs, and keep a bench of proven people so new concepts can start quickly.
  • Direct talent. Brief talent before the shoot, give clear direction on delivery and on-camera performance, and give specific notes on the takes you receive.
  • Direct raw footage. Review raw footage, choose the usable takes and moments, and tell editors which hooks, lines and sections to build the cut around.
  • Direct the creative team. Brief editors and designers with a clear goal, reference and success measure for each asset, and give written feedback that gets to a finished ad in as few rounds as possible.
  • Analyze creative performance. Read ad-level results for each client, work out why ads won or lost (hook, angle, format, talent, offer), and write down what to repeat, iterate or retire.
  • Set creative priorities. Decide what the team makes next for each client and in what order, balancing iterations on proven ads against new concepts, and keep that list current as results come in.

Using AI to write scripts at volume

You will use AI to draft far more scripts than one writer could produce by hand, and you will be the editor who decides what is good enough to shoot. AI is the first draft. You are the final say.

  • Draft in volume. Use AI to generate many hooks and script variations from the creative angle, customer research, offer and past winning ads.
  • Vary on purpose. Ask for different angles, hook types, formats and lengths, not many copies of one idea, so each batch gives the pod something real to test.
  • Edit every script by hand. Nothing goes to talent or the client without a human read. You cut, rewrite and sharpen each draft so it sounds like a real person talking, fits the brand and is easy to perform.
  • Check every claim. AI can invent facts, results and testimonials. You verify each claim, number and promise against the client's own materials, and you keep scripts within platform ad policy and any client or legal rules.
  • Build the system. Maintain the prompts, reference documents (research, personas, offer, past winners) and script templates your pod uses, and improve them based on which drafts get approved and which ads perform.
  • Close the loop. Label each script by angle and hook type, so performance data shows what to ask AI for next.
  • Know when not to use it. Some concepts, especially ones that depend on a personal story or a delicate topic, are better written by you from scratch.

Writing modular scripts

Every script you write is built from interchangeable sections, so one shoot can produce many ad variations and we can test one element at a time.

  • Write in blocks. Build each script from labeled sections: hook, setup, body, proof, offer and call to action. Each section should work on its own and connect cleanly to the others.
  • Write several hooks and CTAs per script. Pair multiple hooks with the same body, and multiple calls to action with the same close, so editors can mix and match from a single set of footage.
  • Keep sections self-contained. Avoid lines that only make sense in one order, such as references to something said earlier, so any hook can be swapped in without breaking the flow.
  • Brief talent for swaps. Have talent record each hook and CTA in more than one take and in a consistent tone, framing and pace, so the pieces cut together without a visible seam.
  • Name every module. Give each hook, body and CTA an ID and record which combination went into each ad, so results can be traced to the specific element that won or lost.
  • Lock compliance in its own modules. Keep approved claims, required disclaimers and disclosures in fixed sections, and re-check any new combination before it goes out.
  • Use AI on the modules. Ask AI for fresh hook and CTA variations against a body that already works, then edit and approve the ones worth shooting.

Platform and regulatory compliance

Some of our clients work in regulated industries, such as health and wellness, supplements, financial services, legal services, and credit, housing or employment offers. You are the first line of defense: every script and creative direction you give must be written to pass Meta and Google review and to stay within the rules that apply to the client.

  • Know the platform rules. Keep current on both Meta's and Google's advertising policies, including Meta's special ad categories, Google's restricted categories, and the limits each sets on health claims, personal attributes, before-and-after claims, misleading claims and sensitive topics. Write scripts that stay inside both so ads are not rejected and accounts are not restricted. Policies change often, so check them again before each new batch of creative.
  • Know the client's industry rules. For each regulated client, learn the claims, disclosures and disclaimers their industry requires, and write them into the script and the on-screen text, not as an afterthought.
  • Substantiate every claim. Do not write results, savings, health benefits or guarantees that the client cannot back up with documentation. Follow advertising rules on endorsements, testimonials and paid creators, including clear disclosure of paid relationships.
  • Brief talent on what they cannot say. Give creators and on-camera talent a plain list of prohibited claims and required disclosures, and review raw footage for off-script statements before it goes to editing.
  • Get approvals in writing. Route scripts and final ads for client sign-off, and for the client's legal or compliance reviewer where the client requires it. Keep a record of what was approved and when.
  • Hold AI drafts to the same standard. AI tools do not know a client's compliance rules. Check every AI-drafted line against them before it moves forward.
  • Escalate, don't guess. When a claim or format is unclear, raise it with the Traffic Manager and the client instead of publishing and hoping.

You are not expected to give legal advice. You are expected to spot risk early, follow the client's compliance guidance, and bring in the client's legal or compliance contact when needed.

What success looks like

  • First 30 days: you know every client in your pod, have read their research, offer and best-performing ads, and have shipped your first scripts with talent booked for the next shoot.
  • First 60 days: each client has a written creative priority list you maintain weekly, a repeatable brief your editors and designers work from, and a shortlist of talent you have worked with.
  • First 90 days: you run the full loop for your clients without help: analyze results, set priorities, write, direct and hand off. New creative ships on schedule, and you can show which ads came from which learning.

What you bring

  • Experience writing direct-response video scripts and hooks for paid social, with examples you can show.
  • A track record of reading ad-level performance data (hook rate, CTR, CPA or ROAS, frequency) and turning it into clear creative decisions.
  • Experience directing on-camera talent or creators, in person or remotely, and giving useful notes on raw footage.
  • Experience briefing and managing editors and designers, and giving feedback that is specific and kind.
  • Comfort in Meta Ads Manager and a reporting tool such as a spreadsheet or dashboard.
  • Clear writing and good judgment about what to make first when everything feels urgent.
  • Reliable follow-through across several clients at once.
  • Hands-on experience using AI tools to draft and iterate on scripts, and the editing skill to turn those drafts into ads that sound human.

Nice to have

  • Experience with UGC and creator-led ads for ecommerce or lead generation clients.
  • Familiarity with creative testing frameworks and with how Meta delivers and fatigues creative.
  • Basic editing skills, enough to rough-cut a hook or mark up a cut.
  • Experience working inside an agency with several client accounts.

How the role fits

YAMU Media organizes client work into pods. Each pod is built for 5 to 8 clients and pairs a Traffic Manager with a Creative Strategist, supported by video editors and designers. You are the creative lead of your pod. The Traffic Manager owns media buying and the client relationship; you own what the ads say and show.

You will work every week with the Traffic Manager on what the data says, with editors and designers on production, and with talent on shoots. You report to Account Manager.

What is offer

  • Employment type: Freelance
  • Location: Open to LATAM, Africa, Asia, Middle East

jobs.excerpt: OverviewThe Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc.
jobs.description:
Overview

The Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc. (CHAI) is a global health organization committed to our mission of saving lives and reducing the burden of disease in low-and middle-income countries. We work at the invitation of governments to support them and the private sector to create and sustain high-quality health systems.

CHAI was founded in 2002 in response to the HIV/AIDS epidemic with the goal of dramatically reducing the price of life-saving drugs and increasing access to these medicines in the countries with the highest burden of the disease. Over the following two decades, CHAI has expanded its focus. Today, along with HIV, we work with our partners to prevent and treat infectious diseases such as COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis, and hepatitis. Our work has also expanded into cancer, diabetes, hypertension, and other non-communicable diseases, and we work to accelerate the rollout of lifesaving vaccines, reduce maternal and child mortality, combat chronic malnutrition, and increase access to assistive technology. We are investing in horizontal approaches to strengthen health systems through programs in human resources for health, digital health, and health financing. With each new and innovative program, our strategy is grounded in maximizing sustainable impact at scale, ensuring that governments lead the solutions, that programs are designed to scale nationally, and learnings are shared globally.

At CHAI, our people are our greatest asset, and none of this work would be possible without their talent, time, dedication, and passion for our mission and values. We are a highly diverse team of enthusiastic individuals across 40 countries with a broad range of skill sets and life experiences. CHAI is deeply grounded in the countries we work in, with the majority of our staff based in program countries. Learn more about our exciting work:

CHAI is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and is committed to providing an environment of fairness, and mutual respect where all applicants have access to equal employment opportunities. CHAI values diversity and inclusion, and recognizes that our mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people with diverse experience, backgrounds, and culture.

Vaccines Program Overview

To ensure people in low- and middle-income countries have access to effective and affordable immunization, CHAI’s Vaccine Markets Team works with vaccine manufacturers, Gavi, UNICEF, WHO, and other global stakeholders improving availability, affordability, and supply security for existing and future vaccines. In doing this, CHAI is applying the techniques it has used successfully to improve access to HIV/AIDS and malaria treatment: improving market demand transparency for suppliers, partners, donors and financiers, and working closely with individual suppliers to optimize their commercial, costing and pricing strategies in low- and middle-income markets.

The team’s current portfolio spans routine and novel vaccine markets (e.g., hexavalent, measles-rubella, pneumococcal conjugate, oral cholera, HPV and RSV vaccines), as well as support to strengthen a diversified supplier base, including efforts to build sustainable African vaccine manufacturing (AVM).

Position Overview

CHAI is seeking a Program Manager to join its Vaccine Markets Team. Reporting to the Associate Director, Vaccine Markets, the Program Manager will lead a set of market-shaping workstreams with a high degree of independence, from scoping new opportunities through project delivery, and will serve as the team’s point of contact on African vaccine manufacturing. The Program Manager will manage a small team of Associates and collaborate with a broader set of team members on specific projects.

Vaccine market priorities evolve quickly, and a large portion of the team’s work arises from emerging opportunities and partner requests. The role suits an entrepreneurial self-starter who can creatively scope and initiate new work while delivering on ongoing commitments.

Responsibilities

Market shaping

  • Lead vaccine market-shaping workstreams, developing an understanding of global market dynamics and designing interventions through analyses, insights and technical know-how shared with suppliers, governments, and partners (incl. bilateral supplier engagements).
  • Creatively scope and initiate new projects that improve the supply sustainability, affordability, and accessibility of vaccines for low- and middle-income countries.
  • Lead the development of market intelligence on assigned antigens (e.g., HPV and novel vaccines such as dengue and RSV) and its dissemination to global health partners, donors, and vaccine manufacturers.
  • Lead and guide analyses (e.g., demand forecasts, uptake models, coverage analysis, production capacity and pipeline planning) and their translation into presentations and reports that strengthen the business case for vaccine access, inform global policy and build the evidence base for high-impact interventions

African vaccine manufacturing

  • Serve as the team’s point of contact on African vaccine manufacturing, staying current on technology transfers, procurement developments and policy changes.
  • Manage and strengthen relationships with key African vaccine manufacturers, providing market insights and targeted business planning support.
  • Disseminate and tailor CHAI’s AVM supply landscape and analyses to relevant partners, e.g. the World Bank, Gavi Alliance partners and CHAI country teams.
  • Lead regular engagement with the Gates Foundation on AVM and coordinate with Gavi, UNICEF, WHO, Africa CDC and other ecosystem partners, including inputs to policy papers.
  • Act as a thought partner on the evolution of AVM-related programs, and scope supplier-specific or landscape work where warranted.

Partners and team

  • Cultivate and lead relationships with key global health partners, donors, and vaccine manufacturers.
  • Manage and coach junior team members, providing hands-on guidance on technical matters and matching development goals to opportunities.
  • Support donor reporting and the development of concept notes and new proposals.
  • Support strategic initiatives at the global ecosystem level, e.g., understanding key market-shaping trends and defining best practices for different antigen segments.
  • Any other duties as required.

Qualifications

  • Minimum advanced degree with strong academic performance.
  • Minimum 7 years of professional experience in a fast-paced, results-oriented work environment (e.g., strategy consulting, pharmaceuticals, health economics, health financing).
  • Clear strategic and structured thinker with strong problem-solving and analytical skills.

jobs.description:
If you’re passionate about helping people protect what matters most to them at a Fortune 100 company with nearly $70 billion in annual sales, as well as innovating and simplifying processes and operations to provide the best customer value, then Nationwide’s Property and Casualty team could be the place for you! At Nationwide®, “on your side” goes beyond just words. Our customers and partners are at the center of everything we do and we’re looking for associates who are passionate about delivering extraordinary care.

This role does not qualify for employer-sponsored work authorization. Nationwide does not participate in the Stem OPT Extension program.


Job Description Summary

Are you a critical thinker who can analyze complex risk and find insurance solutions that balance customer needs with business goals? If you can take initiative, use both your analytical and creative abilities to make sound decisions and have a desire to help people solve real challenges, we want to hear from you!

Our Excess & Surplus/Specialty (E&S/S) lines allow us to provide insurance that other carriers may not offer. It’s a fast-paced environment in a collaborative, team-oriented culture, working in an always-changing, growing industry.

As an Underwriting Specialist in Contract you determine individual risk acceptability, pricing, coverage, terms and conditions, by developing, analyzing and evaluating information and exposures on risks of a complex technical nature for the assigned line of business. In addition, you’ll achieve production and loss ratio goals with assigned general agents or program managers by reviewing and analyzing claims, loss history and taking appropriate action on accounts. General agent assignments are more complex in terms of coverage and general agent relationships. It’s important to establish and maintain effective relationships with general agents to generate premium dollars and profitability. You will work independently with a high level of authority and judgment. Determining appropriate reinsurance placement, if any, on individual accounts is an important element of this role. We will count on you to foster positive business relationships with co-workers, general agents and reinsurers. You will also assist with research, development and presentation of new products, forms and manuals and have opportunities to assist in the training and mentoring of Underwriters and Underwriting Assistants.

Job Description

Key Responsibilities:

  • Reviews individual risks with assigned agents or programs within assigned territory and either declines or accepts business based upon information necessary to make the decision. The underwriter analyzes, with a high level of technical expertise, exposures to loss, develops an adequate premium charge for the exposure and determines appropriate endorsements and exclusions to address loss exposures for the insurance contract. Within department guidelines, places reinsurance, if any, for the account.

  • Achieves individual production and loss ratio goals within assigned territory through sound territory management and marketing. Achieves production, profitability and service objectives. Quotes, prices and underwrites new and renewal policies and endorsements, primarily for complex or service sensitive accounts. Monitors risk selection and pricing decisions for entire agency plant, both on a book of business and individual account level basis. Works with more complex issues concerning coverage, programs, agents and program managers. The underwriter continually analyzes premium and loss results in their territory or assigned agents by agency, state, major class of business and by program. Continually assess quality of submissions and makes corrective action recommendations. Development and implementation of specific action plans may be required

  • Handles policy maintenance items and other mid-term requests. Reviews endorsement requests and processes necessary changes to the policy. Reviews loss control reports and makes recommendations to the agent and/or changes to the policy. Follows up on outstanding information as required. Reviews claim activity and takes appropriate action. May review agency books of business as well as profit/growth results and trends to recommend and implement action plans.

  • Fosters positive business relationships with general agents through daily contact with assigned agents by developing and maintaining good rapport and resolving agency conflicts. Travels to agency offices as required for audits, training or marketing visits. Entertains agents visiting the Company as required. Assists with development of marketing ideas and strategies for underwriting seminars and other marketing campaigns.

  • Places reinsurance per department guidelines based upon the appropriate use of all reinsurance facilities used by the department, including various treaty semiautomatic and facultative reinsurance. Maintains good working relationship with reinsurers.

  • Markets Nationwide products and services to help drive agency and company results, including all enterprise products that may enhance offerings. Assists agency with strategies for pipeline management, producer development and to develop new business in targeted industries and preferred markets. Responds effectively to assess accounts and develop business propositions that win the business.

  • Other responsibilities as assigned may include program research and development, form development, rate development, technical assistance to Agents, Underwriting Assistants, and other Underwriters. Proactively develops technical and business knowledge through internal and external venues

May perform other responsibilities as assigned.

Reporting Relationships: Reports to Department Manager

Typical Skills and Experiences:

Education: Undergraduate degree preferred. Equivalent work experience will be considered in lieu of a degree.

License/Certification/Designation: Completion of general insurance courses such as CPCU, CIC, AU, ARM, CPIW, CWIS, or ASLI is preferred.

Experience: Six years related experience or five years as an underwriter, excess & surplus lines preferred.

Knowledge, Abilities and Skills: Knowledge of lines underwriting policies, practices and procedures, insurance law and underwriting marketing principles and techniques, rating plans and plan concepts, Treaty & Facultative reinsurance concepts, general agency system and company operations, regulatory issues, the general agency system, market conditions and company operations. Ability to communicate effectively, orally, and in writing, interpersonally with individuals and groups via telephone, fax, e-mail and in person. Demonstrates advanced negotiation skills. Ability to manage the assigned line or lines of business, which may include monitoring of aggregates. Ability to work with the wholesale/general agency distribution system. Ability to analyze insurance risks to determine acceptability including policy language, various commercial rating plans and methodologies, reinsurance. Ability to use/learn job related computer software. Ability to devise business solutions to problems, implement the most appropriate, and monitor its effectiveness. Ability to make decisions with minimal supervision.

Other criteria, including leadership skills, competencies and experiences may take precedence.

Values: Regularly and consistently demonstrates Nationwide Values.

Job Conditions:

jobs.excerpt: Job ID: 18393 Alternate Locations: Newell Brands is a leading consumer products company with a portfolio of iconic brands like Graco®, Coleman®, Oster®, Rubbermaid®, Sharpie® and Yankee Candle® - and 24,000 talented teammates around the world.
jobs.description:
Job ID: 18393

Alternate Locations:

Newell Brands is a leading consumer products company with a portfolio of iconic brands like Graco®, Coleman®, Oster®, Rubbermaid®, Sharpie® and Yankee Candle® - and 24,000 talented teammates around the world. Our culture is built on values in action: Integrity, Teamwork, Passion for Winning, Ownership, and Leadership. We work together to win, grow, and make a real impact—supported by a high-performing, inclusive, and collaborative environment where you can be your best, every day.

We are looking for an experienced Facilities and Site Resilience Engineer to join the Engineering, Reliability & Automation (ERA) team within Global Procurement & Supply Network.

The Lead, Facilities & Site Resilience Engineering serves as the licensed technical authority for facilities, building protection, and site resilience across Newell Brands' manufacturing and distribution network. Working from the center, this role sets facilities standards, provides technical review and support to site and project teams, and builds the resilience programs and business continuity plans that protect physical sites and critical infrastructure. The role also helps ensure projects are scoped, designed, and executed to Newell standards.

The ideal candidate is a licensed Professional Engineer with 7+ years of experience delivering or overseeing facilities projects in manufacturing or industrial environments and is ready to influence at network scale. This individual builds structure where none exists, adopts new technology quickly, and uses AI-enabled workflows to improve the quality and speed of their work.

The PE license anchors the role's authority in design review, peer review, and engagement with authorities having jurisdiction (AHJs) and property insurers. This is a technical leadership role, not a project delivery or design-of-record position.

Top Priorities

  • Site resilience and vulnerability assessments
  • Fire/life safety and facilities standards
  • Technical support and review of capital projects

What You Will Own

Site Resilience & Business Continuity

  • Own site resilience programs across the network, from vulnerability assessment through corrective action and verification
  • Assess sites against ASCE 7-22 wind, snow, and seismic thresholds and FEMA flood zone criteria, translating findings into prioritized mitigation roadmaps
  • Build redundancy strategies for critical utilities, including power, compressed air, chilled water, HVAC, and domestic water
  • Develop facility-focused business continuity plans, escalation frameworks, and recovery time objectives for buildings and critical utilities that sites can execute independently, in partnership with Operations and EHS

Building Protection & Fire/Life Safety

  • Set and maintain global standards for fire suppression, sprinkler, fire alarm, clean agent, and smoke control systems
  • Review design packages, contractor proposals, and AHJ submittals against NFPA 13, 25, 72, and 101 and applicable local codes, challenging gaps with technical authority
  • Define inspection, testing, and maintenance programs and track deficiency closure and compliance across the portfolio
  • Partner with property insurers such as FM Global and with AHJs on loss prevention recommendations and compliance gap closure

Capital Project Support & Technical Review

  • Provide technical review and support to site and project teams on facilities capital projects, from scope definition through closeout, without owning project delivery
  • Review scopes, RFPs, SOWs, design packages, contractor proposals, and bid leveling for roofing, HVAC, building envelope, civil and site work, fire protection, and compressed air
  • Identify proposals that are incomplete, overpriced, or out of specification
  • Develop scope, RFP, and SOW templates and contractor qualification criteria that project teams can reuse across the network
  • Support site teams with contractor selection and performance and help resolve technical issues in the field

Power, Energy & Water Systems

  • Support standby generation, transfer switch, UPS, and backup power deployment, from site preparation through commissioning
  • Lead and support energy programs, including lighting, VFD optimization, power factor correction, and utility incentive capture
  • Support solar, microgrid, and self-generation feasibility work in partnership with the ERA Sustainability pillar
  • Partner with process water engineering on cooling towers, closed-loop treatment, and Legionella prevention

Assessments, Standards & Verification

  • Conduct structured site assessments and engineering peer reviews
  • Maintain site condition scorecards and standards compliance matrices that inform capital planning
  • Define measurement and verification protocols and review results on completed projects to confirm alignment with scope, performance targets, and savings identified in appropriation packages
  • Develop facilities engineering standards and lead updates through the standards publishing workflow
  • Support international projects, working with regional teams to apply Newell standards alongside local codes and AHJ requirements

Financial Ownership & Reporting

  • Review capital justification packages, ROI models, and bid comparison matrices developed by site and project teams
  • Build tools and templates to improve consistency and quality across the network
  • Support three-year capital planning and maintain portfolio-level status reporting that provides senior leaders with clear, decision-ready information

Required Qualifications

  • Active Professional Engineer (PE) license in a U.S. state
  • Bachelor's degree in an engineering discipline such as Mechanical, Civil, Architectural, or Fire Protection Engineering
  • 7+ years of experience in facilities, plant, or infrastructure engineering, including delivering, managing, or overseeing capital projects in an industrial, manufacturing, or distribution environment
  • Working technical command of HVAC, roofing, building envelope, civil, and fire protection systems, with the ability to critically review designs and proposals
  • Experience conducting site assessments, audits, or resilience and vulnerability studies and translating findings into funded action plans
  • Demonstrated experience developing or reviewing contractor scopes, RFPs, and project budgets and holding contractors accountable to scope, schedule, and cost
  • Ability to influence site and project teams through technical credibility and sound engineering judgment without direct authority
  • Working knowledge of NFPA 13 and 25, ASCE 7-22, OSHA 29 CFR, and local AHJ requirements
  • Proficiency in the Microsoft Office suite for project tracking and executive communication
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Ability to travel up to 50%, including international travel as projects require

Highly Valued Differentiators

  • PE license in Mechanical Engineering, particularly HVAC and refrigeration, Civil, Structural, or Fire Protection Engineering
  • Experience with greenfield construction or major facility expansion projects, including design review, construction management, commissioning, and startup
  • Experience with property insurer loss prevention standards, such as FM Global
  • Familiarity with NFPA 72, NFPA 101, NFPA 110, NFPA 70 (NEC), IBC, and CMMS platforms
  • Hands-on experience with measurement and verification, including baseline establishment and post-implementation reporting
  • Experience with on-site power generation, compressed air optimization, or process cooling water systems
  • Experience supporting projects at international sites, including working with non-U.S. codes and standards
  • Regular use of AI tools, Power BI, Power Automate, and SharePoint within engineering workflows
  • CFM, CPE, CEM, or CFPS credential, or NIMS/ICS training

What Sets the Best Candidate Apart

The ERA team is a lean, focused engineering group that values ownership, sound judgment, and a high standard of work product. The right person for this role:

  • Walks a facility, identifies what does not meet standard, and returns with a prioritized, actionable plan
  • Takes ownership of programs and standards and drives them through completion
  • Brings a clear point of view backed by sound engineering judgment and works constructively with site teams, project teams, contractors, and insurers
  • Uses AI and digital tools to improve the speed and quality of their work
  • Reviews vendor proposals with a critical eye and identifies what is missing, overpriced, or out of specification
  • Prepares clear, decision-ready materials that senior leaders can use without reformatting
  • Asks the right questions upfront and brings solutions along with identified problems

Newell Brands (NASDAQ: NWL) is a leading global consumer goods company with a strong portfolio of well-known brands, including Rubbermaid, Sharpie, Graco, Coleman, Rubbermaid Commercial Products, Yankee Candle, Paper Mate, FoodSaver, Dymo, EXPO, Elmer’s, Oster, NUK, Spontex and Campingaz. We are focused on delighting consumers by lighting up everyday moments. Newell Brands and its subsidiaries are Equal Opportunity Employers and comply with applicable employment laws. EOE/M/F/Vet/Disabled are encouraged to apply.

JumpCloud® is the AI-powered unified IT management platform designed to secure the modern workforce. JumpCloud is Intelligent, Secure IT.

JumpCloud is a comprehensive cloud directory platform solving complex IT and cybersecurity challenges for organizations worldwide. Because our platform offers immense expansion potential, we need a revenue-focused leader who thrives in technically advanced environments, is genuinely fascinated by the cybersecurity landscape, and brings a track record of selling or expanding technical products. In this role, you’ll be an active, hands-on leader who leads from the front.   • Strong ability to inspire all levels of your team.

  • Creative problem solving ability to identify obstacles and viable solutions

To be considered for a role at JumpCloud®, you will be required to speak and write in English fluently. Any additional language requirements will be included in the details of the job description.

Why JumpCloud?

If you thrive working in a fast, SaaS-based environment and you are passionate about solving challenging technical problems, we look forward to hearing from you! JumpCloud® is an incredible place to share and grow your expertise! You’ll work with amazing talent across each department who are passionate about our mission. We’re out of the box thinkers, so your unique ideas and approaches for conceiving a product and/or feature will be welcome. You’ll have a voice in the organization as you work with a seasoned executive team, a supportive board and in a proven market that our customers are excited about.
One of JumpCloud®'s three core values is to “Build Connections.” To us that means creating " human connection with each other regardless of our backgrounds, orientations, geographies, religions, languages, gender, race, etc. We care deeply about the people that we work with and want to see everyone succeed." - Rajat Bhargava, CEO

Company Mission

At RestaurantSupply.com, our mission is to help customers save time and money when purchasing commercial kitchen equipment and supplies. Role Overview

We are looking for a Senior Full Stack PHP Developer to own the architecture and development of our product catalogue and quoting platform. This is an opportunity to build a new product from the ground up, establish its technical foundations, and shape how we manage and present complex product information at scale.The platform will power our product catalogue and quoting capabilities, bringing together product information from manufacturers and other sources into a structured, reliable, and scalable system.

Your primary focus will be product information management (PIM), data modeling, large-scale data ingestion, and building a maintainable, monitorable, and scalable application. You'll design systems that can ingest, normalize, validate, and manage millions of product records while supporting accurate product information and flexible quoting functionality.You'll work primarily with PHP and Symfony on the backend, using caching, queues, and asynchronous processing to support reliable performance at scale. You'll also build web crawling and scraping capabilities, develop REST APIs, and contribute to a modern JavaScript frontend using React.This is a hands-on engineering role. You'll own both architecture and implementation, working alongside our existing developers and collaborating with colleagues responsible for reviewing product data. We're looking for someone who combines strong technical judgment with attention to detail, curiosity, and a sense of ownership.

Responsibilities

Architecture and Product Development

  • Own the technical architecture of the product catalogue and quoting platform, designing for scalability, maintainability, reliability, and observability.

  • Design robust data models for products, variants, specifications, pricing, configurable options, accessories, and discounts.

  • Build and maintain the PHP/Symfony backend, including REST APIs and integrations.

  • Establish development standards, automated testing practices, and architectural patterns that support long-term maintainability.

Product Information Management and Data Ingestion

  • Build scalable processes for initial imports, incremental updates, and ongoing product data maintenance.

Backend Engineering and Reliability

  • Implement asynchronous processing and background jobs using Symfony Messenger and message queues.

  • Develop caching strategies using Redis or similar technologies while maintaining data consistency.

  • Design robust failure handling, retries, and recovery processes for ingestion pipelines and background workers.

  • Implement monitoring, logging, metrics, error tracking, and alerting to maintain production reliability.

  • Identify performance bottlenecks and continuously improve application performance and resource utilization.

Quoting and Frontend Development

  • Build quoting functionality that supports projects, line items, pricing, markup, and customer-ready quotes.

  • Develop and maintain REST APIs that support the catalogue and quoting experience.

  • Build customer-facing and internal interfaces using modern JavaScript, with React preferred.

  • Collaborate with internal stakeholders to translate product data requirements and quoting workflows into practical technical solutions.

Collaboration and Continuous Improvement

  • Work closely with existing developers and colleagues responsible for reviewing product information.

  • Take ownership of technical challenges from initial design through implementation, deployment, and ongoing optimization.

  • Identify opportunities to simplify workflows, improve data quality, and reduce operational complexity.

  • Evaluate and use AI coding tools and other technologies where they can improve development efficiency and product quality.

Qualifications and Requirements

Required

  • At least 5 years of professional software development experience.

  • Expert-level hands-on experience with PHP 8 and Symfony.

  • Proven experience building or maintaining product information management (PIM) systems, product catalogue platforms, or comparable product data platforms.

  • Experience designing and operating large-scale data ingestion pipelines, ideally involving 1 million or more records.

  • Strong data modeling skills and deep experience with relational databases such as PostgreSQL and ORM frameworks such as Doctrine.

  • Hands-on experience with asynchronous processing, message queues, and background jobs.

  • Strong knowledge of caching systems such as Redis.

  • Experience building reliable web crawling and scraping systems.

  • Solid experience designing and consuming REST APIs.

  • Practical experience with production monitoring, logging, error tracking, and troubleshooting.

  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to take ownership of complex technical challenges.

Nice to Have

  • Experience building quoting, CPQ (configure, price, quote), or product configuration software.

  • Experience working with complex ecommerce product catalogues, manufacturer data, or product feeds.

  • Experience with React and modern JavaScript development.

  • Experience with automated testing and CI/CD pipelines.

  • Familiarity with AI-assisted product data enrichment or classification.

  • Knowledge of commercial kitchen equipment, foodservice supplies, or the broader equipment distribution industry.

  • Comfortable using AI coding tools to improve development productivity.

Personal Qualities

  • Exceptional attention to detail, particularly when working with complex product data.

  • Analytical and systems-oriented thinking.

  • Creative problem-solving and a willingness to challenge inefficient approaches.

  • Strong sense of ownership and accountability.

  • Ability to learn new systems and business domains quickly.

  • Collaborative working style and openness to feedback.

Working Hours

This is a full-time, remote position open to candidates based in Europe.

You must be able to maintain regular working-hour overlap with our team between 10:00 a.m. and 7:00 p.m. Paris time (CET in winter and CEST in summer).

Why Work With Us?

At RestaurantSupply.com, you'll have the opportunity to build a business-critical product from the ground up and directly influence its architecture, capabilities, and long-term direction.

You'll work on meaningful engineering challenges involving complex product data, large-scale ingestion, automation, and quoting workflows. Your work will directly support our ecommerce operations and help improve how customers discover products and purchase commercial kitchen equipment.

We value ownership, practical problem-solving, collaboration, and continuous improvement. You'll have the opportunity to contribute ideas, make technical decisions, and see the impact of your work across the business.

Perks and Benefits

  • Fully remote work from anywhere within Europe, subject to the applicable employment arrangement.

  • Meaningful ownership of a new product and its technical architecture.

  • Challenging engineering work involving large-scale data and real business problems.

  • A collaborative environment where new ideas and better solutions are encouraged.

  • Excellent organizational, prioritization, communication, and interpersonal skills
  • An ability to think innovatively and creatively
  • Team player and strong collaboration skills

  • Experience with web integration using Rest APIs
  • Experience in AI or Atlassian Rovo
  • Experience in other tools including Gitlab, , SNOW and serviceNow

jobs.title: Project Manager II (Germany)
jobs.excerpt: DescriptionThe project manager II has the overall responsibility for the successful initiation, planning, execution, monitoring, controlling and closure of assigned clinical trials.
jobs.description:
Description

The project manager II has the overall responsibility for the successful initiation, planning, execution, monitoring, controlling and closure of assigned clinical trials. The project manager II oversees and coordinates study resources to ensure compliance with the study budget, project scope and timelines and in accordance with applicable standard operating procedures (SOPs), good clinical practices, regulatory and study-specific requirements. Project Manager II acts as the main line of communication to relevant stakeholders and provides input to feasibility, study design, budget development and ensures progress reporting (resources, budget and timeline)

This role will be perfect for you if:

  • You want to work for a mid-sized CRO that works on significant multisite trials, including Global Phase III projects
  • You are looking to position yourself in an environment where you can grow your career alongside the company

IMPACT AND RESPONSIBILITIES

﻿Client interactions

  • Serve as primary contact for the Sponsor
  • Provide efficient and timely updates on trial progress
  • Lead client calls effectively

Project planning

  • Oversee and actively participates in the preparation of project deliverables such as; study plans, protocol, informed consent form, electronic case report form (eCRF), tables/listings/figures (TLFs), clinical study report.
  • Participate in the planning and conduct of the Investigator’s Meeting.
  • Ensure that each site has the necessary material to adequately perform the study (e.g., investigational product, study supplies, special equipment, safety lab kits, etc.).
  • Lead study start-up activities including trial kick-off, TMF setup, site selection and activation, vendor set-up timelines, and site contracting and budgeting.
  • Collaborate with Regulatory Affairs to ensure timely submissions and completeness of essential documents prior to site initiation and throughout the study.
  • Partner with Data Management to ensure CRF alignment with protocol and sponsor requirements, and that data review, query resolution, and database lock timelines are met.

Quality and risk management

  • Ensure assigned studies are “audit ready” at all times.
  • Monitor the quality of study deliverables, (including vendor and SubCRO deliverables) and address issues as they arise.
  • Manage risk and control measures to assure project quality.
  • Analyze discrepancies between planned and actual results.
  • Review and approve responses to quality assurance audits.

Project budget and timelines

  • Control the project budget, with particular attention to internal hours allocated to all activities.
  • Identify out of scope activities for change orders.
  • Proactively manage operational aspects of the clinical trial including trial timelines, budget, resources and vendors. Coordinate tasks and deliverables from all functional departments involved in the project.
  • Communicate effectively with study team members, functional departments, and senior management.
  • Manage and report on recruitment status and highlight initiatives needed to meet recruitment timelines.

Project team leadership

  • Lead the core project team which may include: Associate Project Managers, Project Coordinators, Project Assistants.
  • Ensure all team members have adequate training on the project.
  • Work closely with vendors and the following internal teams to ensure all tasks and deliverables are completed on time, according to plans and according to applicable standards: Site Selection, Regulatory Affairs, Data Management, Clinical Monitoring, Biostatistics, Scientific Affairs.
  • Define and maintain the project-specific training matrix and ensure training records are kept up to date throughout the study.

Requirements

Education

  • B.Sc. in a related field of study to clinical research

Experience

  • At least 5 years industry experience and a minimum of 3 years in Phase I-III clinical trial project management
  • Experience managing dermatology and/or rheumatology trials
  • Experience leading concurrent multi-centered clinical trials with budgets in excess of $3M USD.
  • Experience managing dermatology trials an asset

Knowledge and skills

  • Excellent knowledge of GCP and ICH standards, FDA and Canadian regulations
  • Excellent knowledge of Microsoft Office suite
  • Excellent oral and written skills in English, French is an asset
  • Excellent communication skills
  • Ability to work in a team environment and establish good relationships with colleagues and sponsors
  • Good problem-solving abilities
  • Good organizational skills
  • Strong ability to carry out different projects and work under pressure while meeting timelines

Our company

The work environment

At Indero, you will work with brilliant and driven colleagues. Our values are collaboration, innovation, reliability, and responsiveness. We offer a stimulating work environment and attractive advancement opportunities.

Work location

Note that this opening is for a home-based position in Germany

About Indero

Indero is a contract research organization (CRO) specialized in dermatology. Since its beginnings in 2000, our organization has benefited from a solid reputation for the quality of its research and services exceeding the expectations of its clients. Based in Montreal, Indero continues to grow and expand in North America and Europe.

Indero is committed to providing equitable treatment and equal opportunity to all individuals. As such, Indero will provide accommodations throughout the recruitment and selection process to applicants with disabilities, upon request.

Indero only accepts applicants who can legally work in Germany.
